There was a young man from Bethlehem in Judah’s district, from Judah’s kindred. He was a Levite and was sojourning there.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT judges-section-17-v17-8]

The man left the city of Judah, Bethlehem, to sojourn wherever he could find a place. Traveling on his way, he reached Ephraim’s hill country, Micah’s house.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT judges-section-17-v17-9]
Judges 17:9
Micah said to him, “Where do you come from?” He said to him, “I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah, and I am going to sojourn wherever I find a place.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT judges-section-17-v17-10]
Judges 17:10
Micah said to him, “Dwell with me and be a father and priest to me; I will give you ten pieces of silver for the year, a pair of garments, and provisions for your living.” And the Levite went
[/UNIT]

[UNIT judges-section-17-v17-11]
Judges 17:11
and began to sojourn with the man, and the young man became like one of his sons.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT judges-section-17-v17-12]

Micah filled the Levite’s hand. The young man became his priest and stayed in Micah’s house.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT judges-section-17-v17-13]
Judges 17:13
Micah said, “Now I know that the Lord has done good to me, because the Levite has become my priest.”

But arise, let us go up against them; for we have found the land, and behold, it is very good. Do you remain silent? Do not delay to go in and inherit the land.

[UNIT judges-section-19-v19-17]

Take counsel about her among yourselves and speak.’”

[UNIT judges-section-20-v20-48]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT judges-section-21-v21-22]

=== Ruth ===

--- Ruth 1 ---

[UNIT ruth-section-1-v1-1]
Ruth 1:1
When the judges were judging, there was a famine in the land. A man went from Bethlehem of Judah to live for a time in the field of Moab, with his wife and his sons.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-1-v1-2]
Ruth 1:2
The man's name was Abimelech, and his wife's name was Naomi. His two sons were named Mahlon and Chilion. They were Ephrathites from Bethlehem of Judah. They came into the field of Moab and stayed there.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-1-v1-3]
Ruth 1:3
And Abimelech, Naomi's husband, died, and she was left with her two sons.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-1-v1-4]
Ruth 1:4
They took Moabite wives for themselves: one was named Orpah, and the second Ruth. They lived there about ten years.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-1-v1-5]
Ruth 1:5
And both Mahlon and Chilion also died, and the woman was left bereft of her husband and her two sons.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-1-v1-6]
Ruth 1:6
She arose with her two daughters-in-law, and they returned from the field of Moab, for they had heard in the field of Moab that the Lord had visited His people to give them bread.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-1-v1-7]
Ruth 1:7
She left the place where she had been, with her two daughters-in-law, and they set out on the road to return to the land of Judah.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-1-v1-8]
Ruth 1:8
Naomi said to her daughters-in-law, “Go now, each of you return to her mother's house. May the Lord show you mercy, as you have shown mercy to the dead and to me.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-1-v1-9]
Ruth 1:9
May the Lord grant this to you, and may each of you find rest in the house of her husband.” She kissed them tenderly, and they lifted up their voice and wept.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-1-v1-10]
Ruth 1:10
They said to her, “We are returning with you to your people.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-1-v1-11]
Ruth 1:11
But Naomi said, “Return now, my daughters. Why are you going with me? Do I still have sons in my womb who could become your husbands?
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-1-v1-12]
Ruth 1:12
Return now, my daughters, for I have grown too old to have a husband. Even if I said that I had hope of having a husband and would bear sons,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-1-v1-13]
Ruth 1:13
would you wait for them until they were grown? Would you hold yourselves back for them and remain without a husband? No, my daughters; it has become more bitter for me than for you, because the hand of the Lord has gone out against me.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-1-v1-14]
Ruth 1:14
They lifted up their voice and wept again. Orpah kissed her mother-in-law tenderly and returned to her people, but Ruth followed her.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-1-v1-15]
Ruth 1:15
Naomi said to Ruth, “Behold, your sister-in-law has returned to her people and her gods. You too should return after your sister-in-law.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-1-v1-16]
Ruth 1:16
But Ruth said, “Do not oppose me by making me leave you or turn back from following you, for wherever you go, I will go, and wherever you lodge, I will lodge. Your people are my people, and your God my God.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-1-v1-17]
Ruth 1:17
Where you die, I will die, and there I shall be buried. May the Lord do these things to me, and add these things, for death shall part me and you.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-1-v1-18]
Ruth 1:18
When Naomi saw that Ruth was firmly resolved to go with her, she said no more to her.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-1-v1-19]
Ruth 1:19
The two journeyed until they came to Bethlehem. The whole city resounded because of them, and they said, “Is this Naomi?”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-1-v1-20]
Ruth 1:20
She said to them, “Do not call me Naomi; call me Bitter, for the Sufficient One has dealt very bitterly with me.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-1-v1-21]
Ruth 1:21
I went out full, and the Lord has brought me back empty. Why do you call me Naomi? The Lord has humbled me, and the Sufficient One has afflicted me.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-1-v1-22]
Ruth 1:22
So Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabite, her daughter-in-law, returned from the field of Moab. They came to Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest.
[/UNIT]

--- Ruth 2 ---

[UNIT ruth-section-2-v2-2]

[UNIT ruth-section-2-v2-7]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-2-v2-8]

[UNIT ruth-section-2-v2-9]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-2-v2-10]
Ruth 2:10

[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-2-v2-11]
Ruth 2:11
Boaz answered her, “I have been fully told all that you have done for your mother-in-law since your husband's death: how you left your father and mother and the land of your birth, and came to a people you had not known before.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-2-v2-12]
Ruth 2:12

[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-2-v2-13]
Ruth 2:13
She said, “May I find favour in your eyes, my lord, for you have comforted me and spoken to the heart of your handmaid. And behold, I shall be as one of your maidservants.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-2-v2-14]
Ruth 2:14
Boaz said to her, “It is time to eat now. Come here, eat some bread, and dip your morsel in the vinegar.” Ruth sat beside the reapers, and Boaz heaped barley meal for her. She ate and was filled, and left some over.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-2-v2-15]
Ruth 2:15
She arose to glean, and Boaz commanded his servants, “Let her glean even among the sheaves, and do not put her to shame.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-2-v2-16]
Ruth 2:16
Be sure to carry some for her, and be sure to cast some for her from the heaped-up grain. Leave it, and she shall glean, and you shall not rebuke her.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-2-v2-17]
Ruth 2:17
And she gleaned in the field until evening, and beat out what she had gleaned; and it was about an oiphi of barley.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-2-v2-18]
Ruth 2:18
She lifted it up and entered the city, and her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned. Ruth brought out and gave her what she had left from the food that had filled her.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-2-v2-19]
Ruth 2:19
Her mother-in-law said to her, “Where have you gleaned today, and where have you worked? Blessed be the man who took notice of you.” Ruth told her mother-in-law where she had worked, and said, “The name of the man with whom I worked today is Boaz.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-2-v2-20]
Ruth 2:20
Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, “Blessed is he of the Lord, for he has not forsaken his mercy toward the living and the dead.” And Naomi said to her, “The man is near to us; he is among those who act as our next of kin.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-2-v2-21]
Ruth 2:21
Ruth said to her mother-in-law, “He also said to me, ‘Stay close to my servants until they have finished all my harvest.’”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-2-v2-22]
Ruth 2:22
Naomi said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, “It is good, daughter, that you went with his maidens, and they shall not meet you in another field.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-2-v2-23]
Ruth 2:23
Ruth stayed close to the maidens of Boaz, gleaning until the barley and wheat harvest was over. And she lived with her mother-in-law.
[/UNIT]

--- Ruth 4 ---

[UNIT ruth-section-4-v4-1]

[UNIT ruth-section-4-v4-2]

[UNIT ruth-section-4-v4-3]

[UNIT ruth-section-4-v4-4]

There is no one besides you to act as next of kin, and I come after you.” He said, “I am he; I will act as next of kin.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-4-v4-5]

[UNIT ruth-section-4-v4-6]

Ruth 4:7

[UNIT ruth-section-4-v4-8]

[UNIT ruth-section-4-v4-10]
Ruth 4:10

[UNIT ruth-section-4-v4-11]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-4-v4-14]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-4-v4-15]
Ruth 4:15
He shall be a restorer of life to you and a nourisher of your old age, for your daughter-in-law who loved you has borne him, and she is better to you than seven sons.”

[UNIT ruth-section-4-v4-16]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT ruth-section-4-v4-17]

=== 1 Samuel ===

--- 1 Samuel 1 ---

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-1-v1-1]
1 Samuel 1:1
There was a man from Armathaim Sipha in the hill country of Ephraim. His name was Elkanah, son of Jerahmeel, son of Elihu, son of Thoke, in Nasib Ephraim.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-1-v1-2]
1 Samuel 1:2
He had two wives. One was named Hannah, and the second was named Peninnah. Peninnah had children, but Hannah had no child.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-1-v1-3]
1 Samuel 1:3
The man went up year by year from his city, from Armathaim, to bow down and sacrifice to the Lord God Sabaoth at Shiloh. Eli and his two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, were there as priests of the Lord.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-1-v1-4]
1 Samuel 1:4
When the day came and Elkanah sacrificed, he gave portions to Peninnah his wife and to her sons and daughters.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-1-v1-5]
1 Samuel 1:5
To Hannah he gave one portion, because she had no child. Yet Elkanah loved Hannah more than this other woman, and the Lord had closed her womb.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-1-v1-6]
1 Samuel 1:6
For the Lord had not given her a child, in her affliction and in the despondency of her affliction. She was despondent because of this: the Lord had shut her womb so as not to give her a child.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-1-v1-7]
1 Samuel 1:7
He would do this year after year when she went up to the Lord’s house, and she would be despondent and weep and not eat.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-1-v1-8]
1 Samuel 1:8
Elkanah her husband said to her, “Hannah.” She said to him, “Here I am, my lord.” He said to her, “What is the matter, that you are weeping? Why do you not eat? Why does your heart strike you? Am I not better to you than ten children?”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-1-v1-9]
1 Samuel 1:9
Hannah arose after they had eaten at Shiloh and stood before the Lord. Eli the priest was sitting on the seat by the doorposts of the Lord’s sanctuary.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-1-v1-10]
1 Samuel 1:10
She was in anguish of soul and prayed to the Lord, weeping abundantly.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-1-v1-11]
1 Samuel 1:11
She vowed a vow to the Lord, saying, “Adonai, Lord, Eloai Sabaoth, if Thou wilt indeed look upon Thy handmaid’s humiliation and remember me, and give Thy handmaid male offspring, then I will give him before Thee as a gift until the day of his death. He shall drink neither wine nor intoxicating drink, and no iron shall come upon his head.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-1-v1-12]
1 Samuel 1:12
As she continued praying before the Lord, Eli the priest watched her mouth.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-1-v1-13]
1 Samuel 1:13
She was speaking in her heart, and her lips moved, but her voice was not heard. Eli considered her drunk.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-1-v1-14]
1 Samuel 1:14
Eli’s servant said to her, “How long will you be drunk? Put away your wine and leave the Lord’s presence.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-1-v1-15]
1 Samuel 1:15
Hannah answered and said, “No, my lord. I am a woman whose day is hard. I have drunk neither wine nor intoxicating drink, and I am pouring out my soul before the Lord.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-1-v1-16]
1 Samuel 1:16
Do not regard your handmaid as a pestilent daughter, for I have continued until now out of the abundance of my murmuring.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-1-v1-17]
1 Samuel 1:17
Eli answered her, “Go in peace. May the God of Israel grant the whole request you have made of Him.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-1-v1-18]
1 Samuel 1:18
She said, “Your handmaid has found favour in your eyes.” The woman went her way, entered her lodging, ate with her husband, and drank. Her face no longer fell.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-1-v1-19]
1 Samuel 1:19
They rose early in the morning, bowed down to the Lord, and went on their way. Elkanah entered his house at Armathaim and knew Hannah his wife, and the Lord remembered her,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-1-v1-20]
1 Samuel 1:20
and she conceived. When the time had come, she bore a son. She called his name Samuel and said, “For I asked him of the Lord God Sabaoth.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-1-v1-21]
1 Samuel 1:21
The man Elkanah went up with all his household to sacrifice at Shiloh the yearly sacrifice, his vow offerings, and all the tithes of his land.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-1-v1-22]
1 Samuel 1:22
Hannah did not go up with him, for she said to her husband, “Not until the child goes up, when I have weaned him. He will appear before the Lord and remain there for ever.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-1-v1-23]
1 Samuel 1:23
Elkanah her husband said to her, “Do what is good in your eyes. Stay until you have weaned him. But may the Lord establish what has come from your mouth.” The woman stayed and nursed her son until she weaned him.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-1-v1-24]
1 Samuel 1:24
She went up with him to Shiloh, with a three-year-old calf, loaves, an oiphi of fine flour, and a nebel of wine. She entered the Lord’s house at Shiloh, and the child was with them.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-1-v1-25]
1 Samuel 1:25
They brought him before the Lord, and his father slaughtered the sacrifice that he made year by year to the Lord. He brought the child forward and slaughtered the calf. Hannah, the child’s mother, brought him to Eli
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-1-v1-26]
1 Samuel 1:26
and said, “Please, my lord! As your soul lives, I am the woman who stood before you when praying to the Lord.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-1-v1-27]
1 Samuel 1:27
For this child I prayed, and the Lord gave me my request that I asked of Him.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-1-v1-28]
1 Samuel 1:28
I too lend him to the Lord for all the days that he lives, as a loan to the Lord.”
[/UNIT]

--- 1 Samuel 2 ---

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-1]
1 Samuel 2:1
She said, “My heart is established in the Lord;
my horn is exalted in my God.
My mouth is opened wide against enemies;
I rejoice in Thy salvation.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-2]
1 Samuel 2:2
For there is none holy like the Lord, and there is none righteous like our God;
there is none holy besides Thee.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-3]
1 Samuel 2:3
Do not boast, and do not speak loftily;
let no grandiose speech come from your mouth.
For the Lord is a God of knowledge, and a God who prepares His undertakings.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-4]
1 Samuel 2:4
The bow of the mighty has grown weak, but those who were weak have girded themselves with strength.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-5]
1 Samuel 2:5
Those who were full of bread have been diminished, but the hungry have left the land.
For the barren woman has borne seven, while she who had many children has grown weak.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-6]
1 Samuel 2:6
The Lord puts to death and gives life;
He brings down to Hades and brings up.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-7]
1 Samuel 2:7
The Lord makes poor and makes rich;
He humbles and raises high.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-8]
1 Samuel 2:8
He raises the needy from the earth and lifts the poor from the dung heap, to seat them with rulers of peoples and grant them a throne of glory as their inheritance,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-9]
1 Samuel 2:9
granting a prayer to the one who prays, and He has blessed the years of the righteous one;
for a man is not mighty by strength.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-10]
1 Samuel 2:10
The Lord will weaken His opponent;
the Lord is holy.
Let the wise person not boast in his wisdom, nor the mighty person in his might, nor the rich person in his riches.
Rather, let the one who boasts boast in this: understanding and knowing the Lord, and doing judgment and righteousness in the midst of the earth.
The Lord ascended into the heavens and thundered.
He will judge the earth’s extremities, and He gives strength to our kings and will raise high the horn of His anointed.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-11]
1 Samuel 2:11
They left him there before the Lord and departed to Armathaim, while the child ministered in the Lord’s presence before Eli the priest.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-12]
1 Samuel 2:12
The sons of Eli the priest were pestilent sons who did not know the Lord.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-13]
1 Samuel 2:13
This was the priest’s claimed right from the people, from anyone sacrificing: the priest’s servant would come when the meat was boiling, with a three-pronged meat hook in his hand,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-14]
1 Samuel 2:14
and thrust it into the large cauldron, bronze kettle, or pot. Whatever came up on the meat hook, the priest took for himself. This is what they did to all Israel who came to sacrifice to the Lord at Shiloh.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-15]
1 Samuel 2:15
Before the fat was burned, the priest’s servant would come and say to the man sacrificing, “Give meat to roast for the priest. I will certainly not take from you meat boiled in the cauldron.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-16]
1 Samuel 2:16
The man sacrificing would say, “Let the fat first be burned, as is proper, and take for yourself from whatever your soul desires.” But he said, “No! You must give it now; otherwise I will take it by force.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-17]
1 Samuel 2:17
The servants’ sin was very great before the Lord, for they rejected the Lord’s sacrifice.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-18]
1 Samuel 2:18
Samuel ministered before the Lord, a child girded with an ephoud bar.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-19]
1 Samuel 2:19
His mother made him a little double cloak and would bring it up to him year by year, when she went up with her husband to sacrifice the yearly sacrifice.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-20]
1 Samuel 2:20
Eli blessed Elkanah and his wife, saying, “May the Lord repay you with offspring from this woman in return for the loan you made to the Lord.” The man departed to his place,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-21]
1 Samuel 2:21
and the Lord visited Hannah, and she bore three more sons and two daughters. The child Samuel grew up before the Lord.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-22]
1 Samuel 2:22
Eli was very old, and he heard what his sons were doing to the sons of Israel.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-23]
1 Samuel 2:23
He said to them, “Why do you act according to this report that I hear from the mouth of all the Lord’s people?
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-24]
1 Samuel 2:24
No, children! The report I hear is not good. Do not act this way, for the reports I hear are not good, so that the people do not serve God.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-25]
1 Samuel 2:25
If a man indeed sins against a man, people will pray for him to the Lord; but if he sins against the Lord, who will pray for him?” They would not listen to their father’s voice, for the Lord was firmly resolved to destroy them.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-26]
1 Samuel 2:26
The child Samuel continued to grow and was in favour both with the Lord and with people.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-27]
1 Samuel 2:27
A man of God came to Eli and said, “Thus says the Lord: ‘I clearly revealed Myself to your father’s house when they were in the land of Egypt as slaves to Pharaoh’s house,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-28]
1 Samuel 2:28
and I chose your father’s house from all Israel’s tribes to serve Me as priests, ascend My altar, burn incense, and bear an ephoud. I gave your father’s house all the Israelites’ fire offerings for food.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-29]
1 Samuel 2:29
Why did you look upon My incense and My sacrifice with a shameless eye, and honour your sons more than Me, so that they bless themselves with the firstfruits of every sacrifice of Israel before Me?
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-30]
1 Samuel 2:30
Therefore thus said the Lord, the God of Israel: I said that your house and your father’s house would pass before Me for ever. But now the Lord says: By no means! I will honour only those who honour Me, and the one who despises Me will be dishonoured.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-31]
1 Samuel 2:31
Behold, days are coming when I will destroy your offspring and the offspring of your father’s house,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-32]
1 Samuel 2:32
and no old man of yours will be in My house all the days.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-33]
1 Samuel 2:33
Yet I will not destroy every man of yours from My altar, so that his eyes fail and his soul ebbs away. Everyone remaining in your house will fall by the sword of men.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-34]
1 Samuel 2:34
This will be the sign for you that will come upon these two sons of yours, Hophni and Phinehas: both will die in one day.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-35]
1 Samuel 2:35
I will raise up for Myself a faithful priest who will do everything in My heart and in My soul. I will build him a faithful house, and he will pass before My anointed all the days.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-2-v2-36]
1 Samuel 2:36
The one remaining in your house will come to bow down to him for a silver obol, saying, “Place me in one of your priestly offices, so I may eat bread.”’”
[/UNIT]

[/UNIT]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-3-v3-5]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-3-v3-6]

The Lord called again, “Samuel, Samuel!” He went to Eli a second time and said, “Here I am, for you have called me.” He said, “I have not called you. Return and sleep.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-3-v3-7]
1 Samuel 3:7
This was before Samuel knew God and before the Lord’s word had been revealed to him.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-3-v3-8]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-3-v3-9]
1 Samuel 3:9
He said, “Return and sleep, child. If He calls you, say, ‘Speak, Lord, for Thy servant hears.’” Samuel went and lay down in his place.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-3-v3-10]

The Lord came and stood there. He called him as before, and Samuel said, “Speak, for Thy servant hears.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-3-v3-11]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-3-v3-12]
1 Samuel 3:12
On that day I will raise against Eli everything I have spoken concerning his house. I will begin and bring it to completion.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-3-v3-13]
1 Samuel 3:13
I have told him that I am taking vengeance on his house for ever for his sons’ wrongdoings, because his sons were reviling God, and even so he did not admonish them.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-3-v3-14]
1 Samuel 3:14
I swore concerning Eli’s house: the wrongdoing of Eli’s house shall never be expiated by incense or sacrifices.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-3-v3-15]
1 Samuel 3:15
Samuel lay until morning, rose early in the morning, and opened the doors of the Lord’s house. Samuel was afraid to report the vision to Eli.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-3-v3-16]
1 Samuel 3:16
Eli said to Samuel, “Samuel, child.” He said, “Here I am.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-3-v3-17]
1 Samuel 3:17
He said, “What was the word spoken to you? Do not hide it from me. May God do these things to you, and add these things, if you hide from me a word of all the words spoken to you in your ears.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-3-v3-18]
1 Samuel 3:18
Samuel reported all the words and hid nothing from him. Eli said, “He is the Lord. He will do what is good before Him.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-3-v3-19]
1 Samuel 3:19
Samuel grew, and the Lord was with him, and none of his words fell to the ground.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-3-v3-20]

All Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, knew that Samuel was faithful as a prophet to the Lord.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-3-v3-21]

[/UNIT]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-4-v4-13]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-4-v4-14]

Eli heard the sound of the cry and said, “What is this crying sound?” The man hurried in and reported to Eli.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-4-v4-15]

Eli was ninety years old. His eyes were fixed, and he could not see. Eli said to the men standing around him, “What is the sound of this uproar?”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-4-v4-16]
1 Samuel 4:16
The man hurried up to Eli and said to him, “I am the one who has come from the camp. I fled from the battle line today.” He said, “What happened, child?”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-4-v4-17]
1 Samuel 4:17
The young man answered and said, “The men of Israel have fled before the foreigners. There has been a great slaughter among the people. Both your sons are dead, and God’s ark has been captured.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-4-v4-18]

When the man mentioned God’s ark, Eli fell backward from the seat beside the gate. His back was crushed, and he died, for the man was old and heavy. He had judged Israel twenty years.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-4-v4-19]
1 Samuel 4:19
His daughter-in-law, Phinehas’s wife, was pregnant and about to give birth. When she heard the report that God’s ark had been captured and that her father-in-law and her husband were dead, she crouched and gave birth, for her labor pains turned upon her.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-4-v4-20]

At that time she was dying. The women standing beside her said, “Do not fear, for you have borne a son.” She did not answer, and her heart did not understand.

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-4-v4-21]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-4-v4-22]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-5-v5-4]

[UNIT 1-samuel-section-5-v5-7]

In the eleventh year, in the month of Baal, which is the eighth month, the house was completed in every detail and according to its entire arrangement.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-kings-section-6-v6-2]

The house that King Solomon built for the Lord was forty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and twenty-five cubits high.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-kings-section-6-v6-3]

The porch in front of the temple was twenty cubits long across the house’s width, and ten cubits wide in front of the house. He built the house and completed it.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-kings-section-6-v6-4]
1 Kings 6:4
He made recessed, concealed windows for the house.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-kings-section-6-v6-5]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-kings-section-6-v6-6]
1 Kings 6:6
The lowest side chamber was five cubits wide, the middle six, and the third seven cubits wide; for he left a space all around the house, outside the house, so that they would not take hold of the house’s walls.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-kings-section-6-v6-7]

[/UNIT]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-kings-section-6-v6-10]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-kings-section-6-v6-15]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-kings-section-6-v6-16]

--- 1 Kings 7 ---

[UNIT 1-kings-section-7-v7-1]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-kings-section-7-v7-2]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-kings-section-7-v7-3]

[UNIT 1-kings-section-7-v7-4]

[UNIT 1-kings-section-7-v7-5]

He made two nets to cover the pillars’ capital: one net for one capital and one net for the second capital.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-kings-section-7-v7-6]
1 Kings 7:6

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-kings-section-7-v7-7]

[UNIT 1-kings-section-7-v7-8]

[UNIT 1-kings-section-7-v7-9]
1 Kings 7:9

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-kings-section-7-v7-10]

He made the Sea, ten cubits from brim to brim, round all around and five cubits high; thirty-three cubits in all encircled it.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-kings-section-7-v7-11]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-kings-section-7-v7-12]
1 Kings 7:12
Its brim was made like the brim of a cup, like a lily shoot, and its thickness was a palm.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-kings-section-7-v7-13]
1 Kings 7:13
Twelve cattle were beneath the Sea: three facing north, three facing the sea, three facing south, and three facing east. All their hindquarters faced the house, and the Sea was above them.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-kings-section-7-v7-14]
1 Kings 7:14
He made ten bronze stands. Each stand was five cubits long, four cubits wide, and six cubits high.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-kings-section-7-v7-15]
1 Kings 7:15
This was the construction of the stands: they had enclosed panels, and enclosed panels between the projecting parts.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-kings-section-7-v7-16]
1 Kings 7:16
On their enclosed panels between the projecting parts were lions, cattle, and cherubim, and likewise on the projecting parts. Above and below the lions and cattle were spaces, in descending work.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-kings-section-7-v7-17]
1 Kings 7:17
Each stand had four bronze wheels and bronze attachments; their four parts had shoulders beneath the basins.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-kings-section-7-v7-18]
1 Kings 7:18
The wheels’ arms were in the stand, and the height of each wheel was a cubit and a half.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-kings-section-7-v7-19]
1 Kings 7:19
The wheels were made like chariot wheels; their arms, backs, and assembled work were all cast.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-kings-section-7-v7-20]
1 Kings 7:20
Each stand had four shoulders at its four corners; its shoulders were of one piece with the stand.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-kings-section-7-v7-21]
1 Kings 7:21
At the top of the stand was a round part half a cubit in size, all around at its top, with the beginnings of its arms and its enclosed panels; it opened onto the beginnings of its arms.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-kings-section-7-v7-22]
1 Kings 7:22
Its enclosed panels had cherubim, lions, and palm trees standing, each adjoining the next toward its front, inside and all around.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-kings-section-7-v7-23]
1 Kings 7:23

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-kings-section-7-v7-24]
1 Kings 7:24

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-kings-section-7-v7-25]
1 Kings 7:25
He placed the ten stands, five on the right side of the house and five on the left. The Sea was on the right side of the house, eastward toward the southern slope.

[UNIT 2-kings-section-16-v16-2]
2 Kings 16:2
Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. He did not faithfully do what was right in the eyes of the Lord his God, as his father David had done.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-16-v16-3]
2 Kings 16:3
He walked in the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat, king of Israel. He even led his son through fire, according to the abominations of the nations whom the Lord removed before the Israelites.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-16-v16-4]
2 Kings 16:4
He sacrificed and burned incense at the high places, on the hills, and under every leafy tree.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-16-v16-5]
2 Kings 16:5
Then Raasson king of Syria and Phakee son of Romelias, king of Israel, went up to Jerusalem for war. They besieged Ahaz but could not wage the battle successfully.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-16-v16-6]
2 Kings 16:6
At that time Raasson king of Syria restored Ailath to Syria and expelled the Judeans from Ailath. Idumeans came to Ailath and lived there to this day.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-16-v16-7]
2 Kings 16:7
Ahaz sent messengers to Thaglathphellasar king of the Assyrians, saying, ‘I am your slave and your son. Come up and save me from the hand of the king of Syria and the hand of the king of Israel, who are rising against me.’
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-16-v16-8]
2 Kings 16:8
Ahaz took the silver and gold found in the treasuries of the Lord’s house and the king’s house, and sent gifts to the king.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-16-v16-9]
2 Kings 16:9
The king of the Assyrians listened to him. The king of the Assyrians went up against Damascus, captured it, deported it, and put Raasson to death.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-16-v16-10]
2 Kings 16:10
King Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Thaglathphellasar king of the Assyrians. He saw the altar in Damascus, and King Ahaz sent Uriah the priest the altar’s likeness and design for all its construction.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-16-v16-11]
2 Kings 16:11
Uriah the priest built the altar in accordance with everything King Ahaz sent from Damascus.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-16-v16-12]
2 Kings 16:12
The king saw the altar and went up onto it.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-16-v16-13]
2 Kings 16:13
He burned his whole burnt offering, his sacrifice, and his drink offering, and poured the blood of his peace offerings against the altar.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-16-v16-14]
2 Kings 16:14
He moved the bronze altar that stood before the Lord from the front of the Lord’s house, from between the altar and the Lord’s house, and placed it at the altar’s north side.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-16-v16-15]
2 Kings 16:15
King Ahaz commanded Uriah the priest: ‘On the great altar offer the morning whole burnt offering and evening sacrifice, the king’s whole burnt offering and sacrifice, and the whole burnt offering of all the people, their sacrifice, and their drink offering. Pour all blood of whole burnt offering and all blood of sacrifice against it. The bronze altar shall be for me for the morning.’
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-16-v16-16]
2 Kings 16:16
Uriah the priest did in accordance with everything King Ahaz commanded him.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-16-v16-17]
2 Kings 16:17
King Ahaz cut apart the enclosures of the mechonoth and removed the basin from them. He took the Sea down from the bronze oxen beneath it and placed it on a stone base.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-16-v16-18]
2 Kings 16:18
He built the foundation of the seat in the Lord’s house, and he turned the king’s outer entrance into the Lord’s house because of the king of the Assyrians.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-16-v16-19]
2 Kings 16:19
The rest of Ahaz’s deeds, what he did—are these not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-16-v16-20]
2 Kings 16:20
Ahaz lay down with his fathers and was buried in David’s city. His son Hezekiah became king in his place.
[/UNIT]

--- 2 Kings 17 ---

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-1]
2 Kings 17:1
In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah, Hoshea son of Ela became king in Samaria over Israel, for nine years.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-2]
2 Kings 17:2
He did evil in the Lord’s eyes, though not like the kings of Israel who were before him.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-3]
2 Kings 17:3
Salamanasar king of the Assyrians went up against him. Hoshea became his slave and paid him manaa.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-4]
2 Kings 17:4
The king of the Assyrians found wrongdoing in Hoshea, because he had sent messengers to Segor king of Egypt and had not brought manaa to the king of the Assyrians in that year. The king of the Assyrians besieged him and bound him in prison.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-5]
2 Kings 17:5
The king of the Assyrians went up through the whole land, went up to Samaria, and besieged it for three years.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-6]
2 Kings 17:6
In Hoshea’s ninth year the king of the Assyrians captured Samaria and deported Israel to the Assyrians. He settled them in Alae and Abor, rivers of Gozan, and Ore of the Medes.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-7]
2 Kings 17:7
This happened because the Israelites sinned against the Lord their God, who brought them up from Egypt, from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and they feared other gods.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-8]
2 Kings 17:8
They walked in the ordinances of the nations whom the Lord removed before the Israelites; and Israel’s kings, all who acted so,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-9]
2 Kings 17:9
and all the Israelites who clothed themselves in words that were not so against the Lord their God, built themselves high places in all their cities, from watchtower to fortified city.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-10]
2 Kings 17:10
They set up pillars and groves for themselves on every high hill and under every leafy tree.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-11]
2 Kings 17:11
They burned incense there at all the high places like the nations whom the Lord deported before them. They made associates and engraved, to provoke the Lord.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-12]
2 Kings 17:12
They served the idols, concerning which the Lord had said to them, ‘You shall not do this thing to the Lord.’
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-13]
2 Kings 17:13
The Lord warned Israel and Judah through all His prophets, every seer: ‘Turn from your evil ways and keep My commandments, My ordinances, and all the law I commanded your fathers, all that I sent to them through My servants the prophets.’
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-14]
2 Kings 17:14
But they did not listen. They hardened their back more than the back of their fathers.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-15]
2 Kings 17:15
They did not keep His testimonies by which He warned them. They followed vain things and became vain, and followed the nations around them, concerning whom He had commanded them not to do such things.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-16]
2 Kings 17:16
They abandoned the commandments of the Lord their God. They made a casting for themselves, two heifers, made groves, bowed down to all heaven’s host, and served Baal.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-17]
2 Kings 17:17
They led their sons and daughters through fire, practiced divinations, read omens, and were sold to do evil in the Lord’s eyes, provoking Him.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-18]
2 Kings 17:18
The Lord was very angry with Israel and removed them from His presence. None remained except the tribe of Judah alone.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-19]
2 Kings 17:19
Judah also did not keep the commandments of the Lord their God; they walked in the ordinances Israel had made.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-20]
2 Kings 17:20
They rejected the Lord throughout all Israel’s seed; He shook them and gave them into the hands of those plundering them, until He cast them from His presence.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-21]
2 Kings 17:21
For Israel was apart from David’s house, and they made Jeroboam son of Nebat king. Jeroboam thrust Israel away from following the Lord and caused them to commit a great sin.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-22]
2 Kings 17:22
The Israelites walked in every sin Jeroboam committed; they did not turn away from it,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-23]
2 Kings 17:23
until the Lord removed Israel from His presence, as the Lord had spoken through all His servants the prophets. Israel was deported from its land to the Assyrians, to this day.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-24]
2 Kings 17:24
The king of the Assyrians brought from Babylon the one from Chountha, and from Aia, Aimath, and Seppharouain. They were settled in Samaria’s cities in place of the Israelites, took possession of Samaria, and lived in its cities.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-25]
2 Kings 17:25
At the beginning of their residence, they did not fear the Lord. The Lord sent lions among them, and they killed some of them.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-26]
2 Kings 17:26
They told the king of the Assyrians, ‘The nations you did deport and did resettle in Samaria’s cities do not know the judgment of the God of the land. He has sent lions among them, and behold, they are killing them, because they do not know the judgment of the God of the land.’
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-27]
2 Kings 17:27
The king of the Assyrians commanded, ‘Take away from there; let them go and live there, and they shall enlighten them about the judgment of the God of the land.’
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-28]
2 Kings 17:28
They brought one of the priests whom they had deported from Samaria, and he lived in Bethel. He enlightened them about how to fear the Lord.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-29]
2 Kings 17:29
But each nation made its own gods and placed them in the house of the high places which the Samaritans had made, the nations in their cities where they lived.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-30]
2 Kings 17:30
The men of Babylon made Sokchothbainith; the men of Chouth made Nerigel; the men of Aimath made Asimath.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-31]
2 Kings 17:31
The Evites made Eblazer and Tharthak, and the Seppharouain burned their sons in fire to Adramelech and Anemelech, gods of Seppharouain.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-32]
2 Kings 17:32
They feared the Lord and installed their abominations in the houses of the high places they had made in Samaria, each nation in the city where it lived. They feared the Lord and made priests of the high places for themselves, and performed rites for themselves in the house of the high places.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-33]
2 Kings 17:33
They feared the Lord while serving their own gods, according to the judgment of the nations from which he had deported them.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-34]
2 Kings 17:34
To this day they acted according to their judgment. They fear, and they act according to their ordinances, their judgment, the law, and the commandment which the Lord commanded Jacob’s sons, whom He named Israel.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-35]
2 Kings 17:35
The Lord made a covenant with them and commanded them, ‘You shall not fear other gods, bow down to them, serve them, or sacrifice to them,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-36]
2 Kings 17:36
but only the Lord, who brought you up from Egypt with great strength and a raised arm—Him you shall fear, to Him you shall bow down, and to Him you shall sacrifice.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-37]
2 Kings 17:37
The ordinances, judgments, law, and commandments He wrote for you, you shall take care to perform all the days; you shall not fear other gods.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-38]
2 Kings 17:38
You shall not forget the covenant He made with you, and you shall not fear other gods.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-39]
2 Kings 17:39
But you shall fear the Lord your God, and He will rescue you from all your enemies.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-40]
2 Kings 17:40
You shall not listen to their judgment, which they themselves practice.’
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-17-v17-41]
2 Kings 17:41
These nations feared the Lord while serving their carved images. Their sons and their sons’ sons also do as their fathers did, to this day.
[/UNIT]

--- 2 Kings 18 ---

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-1]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-2]
2 Kings 18:2
He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Abou daughter of Zechariah.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-3]
2 Kings 18:3
He did what was right in the Lord’s eyes, in accordance with everything his father David had done.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-4]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-5]
2 Kings 18:5
He hoped in the Lord, Israel’s God. Among Judah’s kings there was none like him after him, nor among those before him.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-6]
2 Kings 18:6
He clung to the Lord, did not turn away from following Him, and kept His commandments which He commanded Moses.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-7]
2 Kings 18:7

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-8]
2 Kings 18:8
He struck the foreigners as far as Gaza and its boundary, from watchtower to fortified city.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-9]
2 Kings 18:9
In King Hezekiah’s fourth year—which was the seventh year of Hoshea son of Ela, king of Israel—Salamanassar king of the Assyrians went up against Samaria and besieged it.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-10]
2 Kings 18:10
He captured it at the end of three years, in Hezekiah’s sixth year—which was Hoshea king of Israel’s ninth year—and Samaria was captured.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-11]
2 Kings 18:11
The king of the Assyrians deported Samaria to the Assyrians and placed them in Alae, on the Abor, the river of Gozan, and in Ore of the Medes.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-12]
2 Kings 18:12
This was because they did not listen to the voice of the Lord their God but transgressed His covenant, everything Moses the Lord’s servant commanded. They neither listened nor acted.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-13]
2 Kings 18:13
In King Hezekiah’s fourteenth year, Sennacherib king of the Assyrians went up against Judah’s fortified cities and captured them.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-14]
2 Kings 18:14
Hezekiah king of Judah sent messengers to the king of the Assyrians at Lachish: ‘I have sinned. Withdraw from me; whatever you impose on me, I will bear.’ The king of the Assyrians imposed on Hezekiah king of Judah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-15]
2 Kings 18:15

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-16]
2 Kings 18:16

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-17]
2 Kings 18:17
The king of the Assyrians sent Tharthan, Raphis, and Rhapsakes from Lachish to King Hezekiah against Jerusalem with a great force. They went up, came to Jerusalem, and stood at the aqueduct of the upper pool, on the road of the Fuller’s Field.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-18]
2 Kings 18:18
They called to Hezekiah. Eliakim son of Chelkias the steward, Somnas the scribe, and Joash son of Asaph the recorder went out to him.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-19]
2 Kings 18:19
Rhapsakes said to them, ‘Tell Hezekiah: Thus says the great king, the king of the Assyrians: What is this confidence in which you trust?
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-20]
2 Kings 18:20
You said—only words of lips!—“Counsel and strength for war.” Now then, in whom do you trust, that you have broken with me?
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-21]
2 Kings 18:21
Now behold, you have put your trust in this broken reed staff, Egypt. If a man supports himself on it, it enters his hand and pierces it. So is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust him.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-22]
2 Kings 18:22
Since you said to me, “We trust the Lord God,” is He not the One whose high places and altars Hezekiah removed, saying to Judah and Jerusalem, “Before this altar you shall bow down in Jerusalem”?
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-23]
2 Kings 18:23
Now join yourselves to my master, the king of the Assyrians. I will give you two thousand horses if you can provide riders for them.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-24]
2 Kings 18:24
How can you turn back the face of one district governor, one of my master’s least servants? Yet you hope in Egypt for chariots and horsemen!
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-25]
2 Kings 18:25
Now have we come up without the Lord against this place to destroy it? The Lord said to me, “Go up against this land and destroy it.”’
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-26]
2 Kings 18:26
Eliakim son of Chelkias, Somnas, and Joash said to Rhapsakes, ‘Please speak to your servants in Syrian, for we understand it. Do not speak with us in Judean. Why are you speaking within the hearing of the people on the wall?’
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-27]
2 Kings 18:27
Rhapsakes said to them, ‘Has my master sent me to speak these words to your master and to you? Was it not to the men sitting on the wall, who are to eat their own dung and drink their own urine together with you?’
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-28]
2 Kings 18:28
Rhapsakes stood and cried out loudly in Judean: ‘Hear the words of the great king of the Assyrians!
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-29]
2 Kings 18:29
Thus says the king: Do not let Hezekiah lift you up with words, for he cannot rescue you from my hand.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-30]
2 Kings 18:30
Do not let Hezekiah make you hope in the Lord by saying, “The Lord will surely rescue us; this city will certainly not be handed into the hand of the king of the Assyrians.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-31]
2 Kings 18:31
Do not listen to Hezekiah, for thus says the king of the Assyrians: Make a blessing with me and come out to me. Each man shall drink from his vine, eat from his fig tree, and drink water from his cistern,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-32]
2 Kings 18:32
until I come and take you to a land like your own, a land of grain, wine, bread, and vineyards, a land of oil-bearing olives and honey. You will live and certainly not die. Do not listen to Hezekiah, because he deceives you, saying, “The Lord will rescue us.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-33]
2 Kings 18:33
Have the gods of the nations ever rescued, each his own country, from the hand of the king of the Assyrians?
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-34]
2 Kings 18:34
Where is the god of Aimath and Arphad? Where is the god of Seppharouain? And have they rescued Samaria from my hand?
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-35]
2 Kings 18:35
Who among all the gods of the lands has rescued their lands from my hand, that the Lord should rescue Jerusalem from my hand?’
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-36]
2 Kings 18:36
They kept silent and did not answer him a word, for the king had commanded, ‘Do not answer him.’
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-18-v18-37]
2 Kings 18:37
Eliakim son of Chelkias the steward, Somnas the scribe, and Joash son of Asaph the recorder came to Hezekiah with torn garments and reported Rhapsakes’s words to him.

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-19-v19-19]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-19-v19-21]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-19-v19-22]

--- 2 Kings 25 ---

[UNIT 2-kings-section-25-v25-1]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-25-v25-16]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-25-v25-18]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-25-v25-19]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-25-v25-20]
2 Kings 25:20

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-25-v25-23]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-25-v25-24]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-25-v25-25]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-25-v25-26]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-kings-section-25-v25-27]

[/UNIT]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-chronicles-section-9-v9-2]

[UNIT 2-chronicles-section-9-v9-3]

[UNIT 2-chronicles-section-9-v9-5]

[UNIT 2-chronicles-section-9-v9-6]

[UNIT 2-chronicles-section-9-v9-9]

=== 1 Maccabees ===

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-3-v3-1]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-3-v3-2]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-16]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-19]

[/UNIT]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-21]

Jonathan put on the holy robe in the seventh month of the one hundred and sixtieth year, at the Festival of Booths. He gathered forces and prepared many weapons.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-22]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-23]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-24]
1 Maccabees 10:24

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-25]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-26]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-27]

Now continue to keep faith with us, and we will repay you with good things for what you do with us.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-28]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-29]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-30]

I relinquish from today onward the right to receive the third of the grain crop and the half of the fruit of the trees that fall to me, from the land of Judah and the three districts added to it from Samaria and Galilee, from this day and for all time.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-31]

Let Jerusalem and its territory be holy and exempt, free of tithes and dues.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-32]
1 Maccabees 10:32
I also relinquish authority over the citadel in Jerusalem and give it to the high priest, so that he may appoint in it men of his own choosing to guard it.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-33]
1 Maccabees 10:33
Every Jewish person taken captive from the land of Judah into any part of my kingdom I release freely, without payment. Let all remit their taxes, including those upon their livestock.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-34]
1 Maccabees 10:34
Let all festivals, sabbaths, new moons, and appointed days, and the three days before a festival and the three after it, all be days of exemption and release for all Jews in my kingdom.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-35]
1 Maccabees 10:35
No one shall have authority to exact payment from or trouble any of them concerning any matter.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-36]
1 Maccabees 10:36
Let up to thirty thousand men of the Jews be enrolled in the king’s forces, and let allowances be given to them, as is proper for all the king’s forces.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-37]
1 Maccabees 10:37
Some of them shall be stationed in the king’s great strongholds, and some shall be appointed to positions of trust in the kingdom. Their supervisors and commanders shall be from among them, and they shall follow their own laws, as the king has also decreed in the land of Judah.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-38]
1 Maccabees 10:38
Let the three districts added to Judea from the region of Samaria be attached to Judea, so that they may be reckoned under one authority and obey no other authority except the high priest.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-39]
1 Maccabees 10:39
I have given Ptolemais and the territory belonging to it as a gift to the holy places in Jerusalem, for the expenses proper to the holy places.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-40]
1 Maccabees 10:40
I myself give every year fifteen thousand shekels of silver from the king’s accounts, from the appropriate places.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-41]
1 Maccabees 10:41
All the excess that they did not pay from the revenues as in former years they shall from now on give for the works of the house.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-42]
1 Maccabees 10:42
Besides these, the five thousand shekels of silver that they used to take from the revenues of the holy place from its account each year are also remitted, because they belong to the priests who minister.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-43]
1 Maccabees 10:43
All who flee to the temple in Jerusalem and anywhere within its precincts, owing royal dues or any other obligation, shall be released, together with all they possess in my kingdom.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-44]
1 Maccabees 10:44

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-45]
1 Maccabees 10:45
The cost of rebuilding Jerusalem’s walls and fortifying it all around shall be given from the king’s account, and likewise for rebuilding walls in Judea.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-71]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-72]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-73]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-77]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-78]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-79]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-80]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-81]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-82]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-83]

Jonathan burned Azotus and its surrounding towns and took their spoils. He burned the temple of Dagon and those who had fled into it with fire.

Those who had fallen by the sword, together with those burned, numbered about eight thousand men.

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-86]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-87]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-88]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-10-v10-89]

--- 1 Maccabees 11 ---

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-1]
1 Maccabees 11:1
The king of Egypt gathered many forces, like the sand beside the seashore, and many ships. He sought to gain control of Alexander’s kingdom by deceit and add it to his own kingdom.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-2]
1 Maccabees 11:2
He went out to Syria with peaceful words. The people of the cities opened to him and met him, because King Alexander had commanded them to meet him, since he was his father-in-law.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-3]
1 Maccabees 11:3
As Ptolemy entered the cities, he stationed forces as a garrison in each city.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-4]
1 Maccabees 11:4
When they approached Azotus, they showed him the burned temple of Dagon, Azotus and its surrounding towns demolished, the bodies thrown out, and those whom Jonathan had burned in the war. They had piled them in heaps along his route.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-5]
1 Maccabees 11:5
They recounted to the king what Jonathan had done, to bring blame upon him. But the king remained silent.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-6]
1 Maccabees 11:6
Jonathan met the king at Joppa with honour. They greeted one another and lodged there.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-7]
1 Maccabees 11:7
Jonathan accompanied the king as far as the river called Eleutherus, then returned to Jerusalem.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-8]
1 Maccabees 11:8
King Ptolemy gained control of the coastal cities as far as Seleucia by the sea, and devised evil plans concerning Alexander.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-9]
1 Maccabees 11:9
He sent envoys to King Demetrius, saying, “Come, let us make a covenant with one another, and I will give you my daughter whom Alexander had, and you shall reign over your father’s kingdom.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-10]
1 Maccabees 11:10
For I regret giving him my daughter, because he sought to kill me.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-11]
1 Maccabees 11:11
He accused him because he desired his kingdom.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-12]
1 Maccabees 11:12
He took his daughter away from him, gave her to Demetrius, and became estranged from Alexander; their hostility became evident.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-13]
1 Maccabees 11:13
Ptolemy entered Antioch and put on the diadem of Asia. He placed two diadems on his head, that of Egypt and that of Asia.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-14]
1 Maccabees 11:14
King Alexander was in Cilicia at that time, because the people of those places were in revolt.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-15]
1 Maccabees 11:15
Alexander heard and came against him in battle. Ptolemy led out his forces, met him with a strong force, and routed him.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-16]
1 Maccabees 11:16
Alexander fled into Arabia to find shelter there, and King Ptolemy was exalted.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-17]
1 Maccabees 11:17

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-18]
1 Maccabees 11:18
King Ptolemy died on the third day, and his men in the strongholds were destroyed by those in the strongholds.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-19]
1 Maccabees 11:19
Demetrius became king in the one hundred and sixty-seventh year.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-20]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-21]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-22]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-23]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-24]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-25]
1 Maccabees 11:25
Some lawless men from the nation were petitioning against him.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-26]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-27]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-28]

Jonathan asked the king to make Judea, the three districts, and Samaria free from tribute, and promised him three hundred talents.

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-29]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-30]

“King Demetrius to Jonathan his brother and to the nation of the Jews, greetings.

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-31]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-32]

‘King Demetrius to Lasthenes his father, greetings.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-33]
1 Maccabees 11:33
We have judged it good to benefit the nation of the Jews, our friends who keep their obligations toward us, because of their goodwill toward us.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-34]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-35]

The other things belonging to us from now on—the tithes and dues belonging to us, the salt lakes, and the crown payments belonging to us—we grant all these to them.

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-36]

Not one of these provisions shall be annulled from now and for all time.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-37]
1 Maccabees 11:37

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-38]
1 Maccabees 11:38
King Demetrius saw that the land was quiet before him and that nothing resisted him. He dismissed all his forces, each to his own place, except the foreign forces he had recruited from the islands of the nations. All the forces inherited from his fathers became hostile to him.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-39]
1 Maccabees 11:39
Tryphon had formerly been one of Alexander’s men. He saw that all the forces were grumbling against Demetrius and went to Imalcue the Arab, who was bringing up Alexander’s young son Antiochus.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-40]
1 Maccabees 11:40
He stayed with him, urging him to hand the boy over so that he might reign in his father’s place. He reported everything Demetrius had done and the hostility his forces felt toward him, and remained there many days.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-41]
1 Maccabees 11:41
Jonathan sent to King Demetrius, asking him to remove the men of the citadel from Jerusalem and those in the strongholds, because they were fighting Israel.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-11-v11-42]
1 Maccabees 11:42

The people of the city, with their wives and children, went up onto the wall with torn garments and cried in a loud voice, asking Simon to give them his right hand.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-13-v13-46]
1 Maccabees 13:46
They said, “Do not deal with us according to our wickedness, but according to your mercy.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-13-v13-47]

Simon came to terms with them and did not fight them. He expelled them from the city and cleansed the houses in which the idols had been. Then he entered it, singing hymns and blessings.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-13-v13-48]
1 Maccabees 13:48
He removed every uncleanness from it, settled in it men who would carry out the law, further fortified it, and built himself a dwelling in it.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-13-v13-49]
1 Maccabees 13:49
Those in the citadel in Jerusalem were prevented from going out and coming into the country to buy and sell. They became exceedingly hungry, and many of them perished from famine.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-13-v13-50]
1 Maccabees 13:50
They cried to Simon to receive a pledge of peace, and he gave it to them. He expelled them from there and cleansed the citadel from its defilements.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-13-v13-51]
1 Maccabees 13:51
They entered it on the twenty-third day of the second month in the one hundred and seventy-first year, with praise and palm branches, with lyres, cymbals, harps, hymns, and songs, because a great enemy had been crushed out of Israel.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-13-v13-52]
1 Maccabees 13:52
He established that this day should be celebrated every year with gladness. He further fortified the temple mountain beside the citadel, and he and his men lived there.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-13-v13-53]
1 Maccabees 13:53
Simon saw that his son John was a grown man, and appointed him commander of all the forces. He lived in Gazara.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-14-v14-27]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-14-v14-28]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-14-v14-29]

‘Since wars have often occurred in the country, Simon son of Mattathias, a priest of the sons of Joarib, and his brothers exposed themselves to danger and resisted their nation’s adversaries, so that their holy places and the law might stand. They honoured their nation with great glory.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-14-v14-30]
1 Maccabees 14:30
Jonathan gathered their nation, became their high priest, and was gathered to his people.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-14-v14-31]

Their enemies wished to invade their country and stretch out their hands against their holy places.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-14-v14-32]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-14-v14-33]
1 Maccabees 14:33
He fortified the cities of Judea and Beth-zur on Judea’s border, where the enemies’ weapons had formerly been, and stationed Jewish men there as a garrison.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-14-v14-34]
1 Maccabees 14:34
He fortified Joppa by the sea and Gazara on the borders of Azotus, where the enemies had formerly lived. He settled Jews there and provided everything necessary for their restoration.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-14-v14-35]
1 Maccabees 14:35
The people saw Simon’s faithfulness and the glory he had resolved to bring to his nation. They made him their leader and high priest because he had done all these things, because of the righteousness and faithfulness he maintained toward his nation, and because he sought in every way to exalt his people.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-14-v14-36]
1 Maccabees 14:36
In his days it prospered in his hands to remove the nations from their country, including those in the city of David at Jerusalem who had made themselves a citadel. From it they used to go out and defile the surroundings of the holy places, inflicting a great blow upon purity.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-14-v14-37]
1 Maccabees 14:37
He settled Jewish men in it, fortified it for the security of the country and city, and raised Jerusalem’s walls.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-14-v14-38]
1 Maccabees 14:38
King Demetrius accordingly confirmed him in the high priesthood,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-14-v14-39]
1 Maccabees 14:39
made him one of his Friends, and honoured him with great glory.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-14-v14-40]

For he had heard that the Jews had been addressed by the Romans as friends, allies, and brothers, and that they had received Simon’s envoys with honour;
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-14-v14-41]
1 Maccabees 14:41
and that the Jews and priests had agreed that Simon should be their leader and high priest for ever, until a faithful prophet should arise;
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-14-v14-42]
1 Maccabees 14:42
that he should be their general, and take care of the holy places, appointing through his authority those in charge of their works, the country, the weapons, and the strongholds;
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-14-v14-43]
1 Maccabees 14:43
that he should take care of the holy places, be obeyed by everyone, have all documents in the country written in his name, and wear purple and gold ornaments;
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-14-v14-44]
1 Maccabees 14:44
and that no one among the people or priests should have authority to annul any of these things, contradict what he should say, convene a gathering in the country without him, wear purple, or fasten on a golden clasp.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-14-v14-45]
1 Maccabees 14:45
Whoever acts contrary to these provisions or annuls any of them shall be liable.’
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-14-v14-46]

All the people agreed to establish Simon to act according to these terms.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-14-v14-47]
1 Maccabees 14:47
Simon accepted and agreed to serve as high priest, to be general and ethnarch of the Jews and priests, and to preside over them all.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-14-v14-48]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-14-v14-49]
1 Maccabees 14:49
and that copies be placed in the treasury so that Simon and his sons might possess them.”
[/UNIT]

--- 1 Maccabees 15 ---

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-15-v15-1]
1 Maccabees 15:1
Antiochus son of King Demetrius sent letters from the islands of the sea to Simon, priest and ethnarch of the Jews, and to the whole nation.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-15-v15-2]
1 Maccabees 15:2
They contained the following: “King Antiochus to Simon the great priest and ethnarch, and to the nation of the Jews, greetings.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-15-v15-3]
1 Maccabees 15:3
Since certain pestilent men have seized the kingdom of our fathers, I wish to reclaim the kingdom and restore it as it was before. I have recruited a multitude of forces and prepared warships.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-15-v15-4]
1 Maccabees 15:4
I intend to land in the country to pursue those who have ruined our country and devastated many cities in my kingdom.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-15-v15-5]
1 Maccabees 15:5
Now, therefore, I confirm to you all the remissions that the kings before me granted you, and all the other gifts they granted you.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-15-v15-6]
1 Maccabees 15:6
I permit you to strike your own coinage as money for your country.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-15-v15-7]
1 Maccabees 15:7
Jerusalem and the holy places shall be free. All the weapons you have prepared and the strongholds you have built and hold shall remain yours.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-15-v15-8]
1 Maccabees 15:8
Every royal debt and all future royal dues shall be remitted to you from now and for all time.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-15-v15-9]
1 Maccabees 15:9
When we gain control of our kingdom, we will honour you, your nation, and the temple with great glory, so that your glory may become evident throughout the whole earth.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-15-v15-10]
1 Maccabees 15:10
In the one hundred and seventy-fourth year Antiochus went out into the land of his fathers. All the forces joined him, so that only a few remained with Tryphon.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-15-v15-11]

Antiochus pursued him, and he fled to Dora by the sea,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-15-v15-12]
1 Maccabees 15:12
for he knew that evils had gathered against him and that the forces had abandoned him.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-15-v15-13]
1 Maccabees 15:13
Antiochus encamped against Dora, with a hundred and twenty thousand warriors and eight thousand cavalry.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-15-v15-14]
1 Maccabees 15:14
He surrounded the city, and the ships joined the attack from the sea. He pressed the city from land and sea and allowed no one to go out or come in.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-15-v15-15]
1 Maccabees 15:15
Numenius and his companions came from Rome carrying letters to the kings and countries, in which the following was written:
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-15-v15-16]

“Lucius, consul of the Romans, to King Ptolemy, greetings.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-15-v15-17]
1 Maccabees 15:17
The envoys of the Jews, our friends and allies, came to us to renew the friendship and alliance established from the beginning, sent by Simon the high priest and the Jewish people.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-15-v15-18]
1 Maccabees 15:18
They brought a golden shield of a thousand minas.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-15-v15-19]

We therefore resolved to write to the kings and countries that they should not seek their harm or make war on them, their cities, or their country, and should not ally themselves with those making war against them.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-15-v15-20]
1 Maccabees 15:20
We decided to accept the shield from them.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-15-v15-21]

If, therefore, any pestilent men have escaped from their country to you, hand them over to Simon the high priest, so that he may punish them according to their law.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-15-v15-22]
1 Maccabees 15:22
He wrote the same things to King Demetrius, Attalus, Ariarathes, and Arsaces,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-15-v15-23]
1 Maccabees 15:23

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-15-v15-24]
1 Maccabees 15:24
They wrote a copy of these things to Simon the high priest.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-15-v15-25]
1 Maccabees 15:25
On the second day King Antiochus encamped against Dora, continually bringing his forces against it, making siege engines, and blocking Tryphon from going out or coming in.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-15-v15-26]

Simon sent him two thousand picked men to fight alongside him, along with silver, gold, and ample equipment.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-15-v15-27]
1 Maccabees 15:27
He would not receive them, but annulled everything he had previously agreed with Simon and became estranged from him.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-15-v15-28]
1 Maccabees 15:28
He sent Athenobius, one of his Friends, to confer with him, saying, “You hold Joppa, Gazara, and the citadel in Jerusalem, cities of my kingdom.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-15-v15-29]
1 Maccabees 15:29
You have devastated their territories, inflicted a great blow upon the land, and gained control of many places in my kingdom.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-15-v15-30]
1 Maccabees 15:30
Now, therefore, hand over the cities you have seized and the tribute of the places you have taken outside the borders of Judea.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 1-maccabees-section-15-v15-31]
