[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-12-v12-36]
2 Maccabees 12:36
When Esdris’s men had been fighting for a long time and were exhausted, Judas called upon the Lord to appear as their ally and leader of the war.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-12-v12-37]
2 Maccabees 12:37
Beginning the cry with hymns in their ancestral language, he rushed unexpectedly upon Gorgias’s forces and put them to flight.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-12-v12-38]
2 Maccabees 12:38
Judas took his army and came to the city of Adullam. As the seventh day was approaching, they purified themselves according to custom and observed the Sabbath there.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-12-v12-39]
2 Maccabees 12:39
On the following day, when it had become necessary, Judas’s men came to recover the bodies of the fallen and place them with their kinsmen in the ancestral tombs.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-12-v12-40]
2 Maccabees 12:40
Under the tunics of each of the dead they found sacred objects of the idols from Jamnia, things from which the law excludes the Jews. It became clear to everyone that these men had fallen for this reason.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-12-v12-41]
2 Maccabees 12:41
They all therefore blessed the deeds of the Lord, the righteous Judge who makes hidden things manifest,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-12-v12-42]
2 Maccabees 12:42
and turned to supplication, asking that the sin committed might be completely blotted out. The noble Judas urged the multitude to keep themselves free from sin, having seen with their own eyes what had happened because of the sin of those who had fallen.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-12-v12-43]
2 Maccabees 12:43
He took up a collection from each man, amounting to two thousand drachmas of silver, and sent it to Jerusalem to offer a sacrifice for sin. He acted very well and nobly, considering the resurrection.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-12-v12-44]
2 Maccabees 12:44
For if he did not expect those who had fallen to rise again, it would have been superfluous and foolish to pray for the dead.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-12-v12-45]
2 Maccabees 12:45
But if he was looking to the finest reward laid up for those who fall asleep in piety, the thought was holy and devout. Therefore he made atonement for the dead, so that they might be released from their sin.
[/UNIT]

--- 2 Maccabees 13 ---

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-13-v13-1]
2 Maccabees 13:1
In the one hundred forty-ninth year, word reached Judas and his men that Antiochus Eupator had come against Judea with multitudes,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-13-v13-2]
2 Maccabees 13:2
and with him Lysias, his guardian and chief minister, each having a Greek force of one hundred ten thousand infantry, fifty-three hundred horsemen, twenty-two elephants, and three hundred scythe-bearing chariots.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-13-v13-3]
2 Maccabees 13:3
Menelaus also joined them and urged Antiochus on with much deceit, not for his homeland’s deliverance, but thinking that he would be restored to office.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-13-v13-4]
2 Maccabees 13:4
But the King of kings stirred Antiochus’s anger against the accursed man. When Lysias pointed out that he was the cause of all the evils, Antiochus ordered that he be taken to Beroea and destroyed according to the custom of that place.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-13-v13-5]
2 Maccabees 13:5
In that place there is a tower fifty cubits high, full of ashes. It had a revolving device with a sheer drop on every side into the ashes.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-13-v13-6]
2 Maccabees 13:6
There they all push to destruction anyone guilty of temple robbery or notorious for certain other evils.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-13-v13-7]
2 Maccabees 13:7
By such a fate the lawless Menelaus happened to die, receiving not even a place in the earth.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-13-v13-8]
2 Maccabees 13:8
And most justly: since he had committed many sins against the altar, whose fire and ashes were pure, he received his death in ashes.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-13-v13-9]
2 Maccabees 13:9
The king, made barbarous in his intentions, was coming to show the Jews evils worse than those that had occurred in his father’s time.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-13-v13-10]
2 Maccabees 13:10
When Judas learned these things, he ordered the multitude to call upon the Lord day and night, that if ever He had helped them before, He would help them now as they were about to be deprived of the law, homeland and holy temple,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-13-v13-11]
2 Maccabees 13:11
and would not permit the people, who had only just gained a little respite, to fall under the power of blasphemous nations.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-13-v13-12]
2 Maccabees 13:12
All did the same together and entreated the merciful Lord with weeping, fasts and prostration for three days without ceasing. Judas encouraged them and ordered them to assemble.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-13-v13-13]
2 Maccabees 13:13
Meeting privately with the elders, he resolved that before the king’s army entered Judea and gained control of the city, they should go out and decide matters with God’s help.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-13-v13-14]
2 Maccabees 13:14
Entrusting the outcome to the Creator of the world, he urged those with him to fight nobly to the death for laws, temple, city, homeland and civic life. He made his encampment near Modein.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-13-v13-15]
2 Maccabees 13:15
Giving his men “God’s victory” as the watchword, he attacked the royal quarters in the camp by night with selected young men of the finest quality. He killed about two thousand men and stabbed the leading elephant together with the man in its tower.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-13-v13-16]
2 Maccabees 13:16
Finally they filled the camp with dread and confusion and departed successfully.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-13-v13-17]
2 Maccabees 13:17
This had taken place just as day was dawning, because of the Lord’s protection that helped him.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-13-v13-18]

The king, having tasted the Jews’ boldness, tried to take the places by stratagem.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-13-v13-19]

He advanced against Beth-zur, a strong fortress of the Jews; he was routed, repulsed and defeated.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-13-v13-20]

Judas sent necessary supplies to those inside.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-13-v13-21]
2 Maccabees 13:21
Rhodocus, one of the Jewish ranks, disclosed the secrets to the enemy. He was sought out, caught and imprisoned.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-13-v13-22]
2 Maccabees 13:22
The king negotiated a second time with those in Beth-zur, gave a pledge, received one, and went away. He attacked Judas’s men and was defeated.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-13-v13-23]
2 Maccabees 13:23
He learned that Philip, whom he had left in charge of affairs in Antioch, had lost his senses. Disturbed, he appealed to the Jews, submitted and swore to all just conditions. He made a settlement, offered sacrifice, honoured the temple, and treated the place kindly.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-13-v13-24]
2 Maccabees 13:24
He warmly received Maccabeus and left Hegemonides as governor from Ptolemais to the territory of the Gerrhenes.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-13-v13-25]
2 Maccabees 13:25
He came to Ptolemais. The people of Ptolemais were distressed about the agreements, for they were so indignant that they wished to annul the provisions.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-13-v13-26]
2 Maccabees 13:26
Lysias went up to the platform, offered such a defence as was possible, persuaded them, calmed them, won their goodwill, and departed for Antioch. Thus unfolded the events of the king’s expedition and withdrawal.
[/UNIT]

--- 2 Maccabees 14 ---

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-1]
2 Maccabees 14:1
After a period of three years, word reached Judas and his men that Demetrius son of Seleucus had sailed into the harbour at Tripolis with a strong force and a fleet,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-2]
2 Maccabees 14:2
had gained control of the country, and had done away with Antiochus and his guardian Lysias.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-3]
2 Maccabees 14:3
A certain Alcimus, who had formerly been high priest but had willingly defiled himself during the times of separation, realized that there was no way for him to obtain deliverance or regain access to the holy altar.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-4]
2 Maccabees 14:4
About the one hundred fifty-first year he came to King Demetrius, bringing him a golden crown and a palm, and also some of the customary temple branches. That day he remained quiet.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-5]
2 Maccabees 14:5

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-6]
2 Maccabees 14:6
“Those Jews called Hasideans, whose leader is Judas Maccabeus, foster war and rebellion, preventing the kingdom from obtaining stability.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-7]
2 Maccabees 14:7
Therefore, having been deprived of my ancestral honour—I mean the high priesthood—I have now come here,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-8]
2 Maccabees 14:8
first because I am sincerely concerned for the king’s interests, and second because I seek the good of my own fellow citizens. For through the thoughtlessness of those men, our whole people suffer no small misfortune.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-9]
2 Maccabees 14:9
Now that you know each of these things, O king, take thought for the country and our distressed people, in accordance with your readily bestowed humanity toward everyone.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-10]
2 Maccabees 14:10
For as long as Judas survives, public affairs cannot find peace.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-11]
2 Maccabees 14:11
When he had said such things, the other friends who were hostile to Judas quickly inflamed Demetrius further.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-12]
2 Maccabees 14:12
He immediately selected Nicanor, the former commander of the elephants, appointed him governor of Judea, and sent him out,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-13]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-14]

The nations in Judea who had driven Judas into exile joined Nicanor in crowds, thinking the Jews’ misfortunes and disasters would become their own successes.

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-15]
2 Maccabees 14:15
When Judas’s men heard of Nicanor’s advance and the attack of the nations, they sprinkled earth on themselves and entreated the One who established His own people for ever and always assists His own portion by a manifestation.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-16]
2 Maccabees 14:16
When their leader gave the command, he immediately set out from there and met them at a village called Dessau.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-17]
2 Maccabees 14:17
Simon, Judas’s brother, had engaged Nicanor, but had faltered for a time because of the opponents’ sudden silence.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-18]
2 Maccabees 14:18
Nevertheless, Nicanor heard of the courage of Judas’s men and their spirit in struggles for their homeland, and was wary of deciding the matter through bloodshed.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-19]
2 Maccabees 14:19
Therefore he sent Posidonius, Theodotus and Mattathias to give and receive pledges.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-20]

After prolonged consideration of these matters, the leader consulted the multitudes. A unanimous opinion emerged, and they consented to the agreements.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-21]

They appointed a day on which they would meet privately in the same place. A chariot came forward from each side, and they set out seats.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-22]
2 Maccabees 14:22
Judas stationed armed men ready at strategic places, lest the enemy suddenly attempt some treachery. They held an appropriate conference.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-23]
2 Maccabees 14:23
Nicanor remained in Jerusalem and did nothing out of place; he dismissed the crowds that had assembled in throngs.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-24]
2 Maccabees 14:24
He kept Judas continually in his presence, having become deeply attached to the man.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-25]
2 Maccabees 14:25
He urged him to marry and have children. Judas married, settled down and shared in ordinary life.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-26]
2 Maccabees 14:26
Alcimus saw their goodwill toward one another and obtained the agreements they had made. He went to Demetrius and said that Nicanor’s intentions were disloyal to the government, for he had appointed Judas, the kingdom’s conspirator, as his successor.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-27]
2 Maccabees 14:27
The king became furious and, provoked by the thoroughly wicked man’s slanders, wrote to Nicanor, declaring his distress over the agreements and ordering him to send Maccabeus in chains to Antioch immediately.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-28]
2 Maccabees 14:28
When these instructions reached Nicanor, he was dismayed and distressed at the prospect of annulling the settlement when the man had done no wrong.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-29]
2 Maccabees 14:29
But since he could not oppose the king, he watched for a suitable moment to accomplish this by stratagem.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-30]
2 Maccabees 14:30
Maccabeus saw that Nicanor was dealing more harshly with him and that their customary meeting had become less courteous. Recognizing that the harshness had no good cause, he gathered not a few of his men and concealed himself from Nicanor.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-31]
2 Maccabees 14:31
The other man realized that Judas had skillfully outmaneuvered him. He went to the greatest and holy temple while the priests were offering the required sacrifices and ordered them to hand over the man.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-32]
2 Maccabees 14:32
When they declared with oaths that they did not know where the man being sought was,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-33]
2 Maccabees 14:33
he stretched his right hand toward the temple and swore, “Unless you hand Judas over to me in chains, I will make this enclosure of God a level plain, tear down the altar, and erect here a splendid temple for Dionysus.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-34]
2 Maccabees 14:34
Having said this, he departed. The priests stretched their hands toward heaven and called upon the One who continually defends our nation, saying,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-35]
2 Maccabees 14:35
“Thou, Lord of all, hast need of nothing, yet Thou wast pleased that a temple for Thy dwelling should come into being among us.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-36]
2 Maccabees 14:36
And now, holy Lord of all sanctification, preserve this recently purified house undefiled for ever.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-37]
2 Maccabees 14:37
A certain Razis, one of Jerusalem’s elders, was reported to Nicanor: a man who loved his fellow citizens, was very well spoken of, and because of his goodwill was called a father of the Jews.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-38]
2 Maccabees 14:38
For in the earlier times of separation he had incurred a judgment for Judaism, risking both body and soul for Judaism with complete earnestness.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-39]
2 Maccabees 14:39
Nicanor, wishing to make his hostility toward the Jews evident, sent more than five hundred soldiers to arrest him,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-40]
2 Maccabees 14:40
for he thought that by arresting him he would inflict a disaster upon them.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-41]
2 Maccabees 14:41
As the multitudes were about to take the tower, forcing the courtyard door and ordering fire to be brought to set the doors alight, Razis, surrounded, thrust his sword into himself,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-42]
2 Maccabees 14:42
wishing to die nobly rather than fall under the power of the accursed men and be outraged in a manner unworthy of his own nobility.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-43]
2 Maccabees 14:43
But because of the haste of the struggle he did not strike accurately. As the crowds rushed inside the doorways, he ran bravely up onto the wall and hurled himself courageously down into the crowds.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-44]
2 Maccabees 14:44
They quickly drew back, leaving a space, and he fell into the middle of the empty area.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-45]
2 Maccabees 14:45
Still breathing and burning with anger, he rose. Although his blood streamed out and his wounds were grievous, he ran through the crowds and stood on a projecting rock.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-14-v14-46]
2 Maccabees 14:46
By now entirely drained of blood, he pulled out his entrails, took them in both hands and hurled them at the crowds. Calling upon the Master of life and spirit to give these back to him again, he departed in this manner.

--- 2 Maccabees 15 ---

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-1]
2 Maccabees 15:1
Nicanor learned that Judas and his men were in the regions of Samaria and planned to attack them in complete security on the day of rest.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-2]
2 Maccabees 15:2
The Jews who were compelled to accompany him said, “Do not destroy so savagely and barbarously, but assign honour to the day that the One who watches all things has especially honoured with holiness.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-3]
2 Maccabees 15:3
The thrice-accursed man asked whether there was a Sovereign in heaven who had commanded the observance of the Sabbath day.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-4]
2 Maccabees 15:4
They declared, “The living Lord Himself is the Sovereign in heaven, who commanded that the seventh day be observed.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-5]
2 Maccabees 15:5
But he said, “And I am a sovereign on earth, who commands that weapons be taken up and the king’s business carried out.” Nevertheless he did not succeed in accomplishing his cruel intention.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-6]
2 Maccabees 15:6
Nicanor, holding his neck high in all arrogance, had determined to erect a common trophy over Judas and his men.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-7]
2 Maccabees 15:7
But Maccabeus remained continually confident, with every hope of receiving help from the Lord.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-8]
2 Maccabees 15:8
He urged those with him not to fear the nations’ advance, but to remember the help they had previously received from heaven and now expect the victory that would come to them from the Almighty.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-9]
2 Maccabees 15:9
Encouraging them from the law and the prophets, and reminding them also of the struggles they had completed, he made them more eager.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-10]
2 Maccabees 15:10
Arousing their spirits, he gave orders while also pointing out the nations’ faithlessness and violation of their oaths.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-11]
2 Maccabees 15:11
Arming each of them with the encouragement of good words more than with the security of shields and lances, he also related a trustworthy dream, a kind of waking vision, and gladdened them all.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-12]
2 Maccabees 15:12
Its vision was as follows: Onias, the former high priest, a noble and good man, modest in his encounters, gentle in character, speaking fittingly, and practiced from childhood in everything belonging to virtue, stretched out his hands and prayed for the whole community of the Jews.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-13]
2 Maccabees 15:13
Then another man appeared, distinguished by gray hair and glory, surrounded by a wondrous and most magnificent majesty.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-14]
2 Maccabees 15:14
Onias spoke and said, “This is the lover of the brothers, who prays much for the people and the holy city: Jeremiah, God’s prophet.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-15]
2 Maccabees 15:15
Jeremiah stretched out his right hand and handed Judas a golden sword. As he gave it, he addressed him in these words:
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-16]
2 Maccabees 15:16
“Take this holy sword, a gift from God, with which you will shatter the adversaries.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-17]
2 Maccabees 15:17
Encouraged by Judas’s very fine words, which could incite them to virtue and strengthen the young men’s souls, they decided not to campaign, but to charge nobly and, engaging with all courage, decide the matter, because the city, the holy things and the temple were in danger.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-18]
2 Maccabees 15:18
For concern for wives and children, and also brothers and kinsmen, occupied a lesser place with them; greatest and foremost was their fear for the consecrated temple.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-19]
2 Maccabees 15:19
Those confined within the city also had no minor anguish, troubled about the attack in the open country.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-20]
2 Maccabees 15:20
Everyone was now awaiting the coming decision. The enemy had already approached, the army had been drawn up, the beasts positioned at a suitable point, and the cavalry stationed on the wing.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-21]
2 Maccabees 15:21
Maccabeus saw the arrival of the multitudes, their varied equipment of weapons, and the beasts’ savagery. Stretching his hands toward heaven, he called upon the wonder-working Lord, knowing that victory does not come through weapons, but that He obtains it for the worthy as He judges.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-22]
2 Maccabees 15:22
He called upon Him in this way: “Thou, Master, didst send Thine angel in the time of Hezekiah, king of Judea, and he killed about one hundred eighty-five thousand in Sennacherib’s camp.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-23]
2 Maccabees 15:23
Now also, Sovereign of the heavens, send a good angel before us to bring dread and trembling.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-24]
2 Maccabees 15:24
By the greatness of Thine arm, may those who come with blasphemy against Thy holy people be struck with terror.” With these words he ended.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-25]
2 Maccabees 15:25
Nicanor’s men advanced with trumpets and battle hymns.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-26]
2 Maccabees 15:26
But Judas’s men met the enemy with invocation and prayers.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-27]
2 Maccabees 15:27
Fighting with their hands and praying to God with their hearts, they struck down no fewer than thirty-five thousand, greatly gladdened by God’s manifestation.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-28]
2 Maccabees 15:28
When they had finished the engagement and were returning with joy, they recognized that Nicanor had fallen in his full armour.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-29]
2 Maccabees 15:29
Amid shouting and commotion, they blessed the Sovereign in their ancestral language.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-30]
2 Maccabees 15:30
The man who had fought foremost for his fellow citizens with his whole body and soul, preserving the goodwill of his youth toward his countrymen, ordered Nicanor’s head and his hand with the shoulder to be cut off and carried to Jerusalem.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-31]
2 Maccabees 15:31
When he arrived there, he called his fellow countrymen together, stationed the priests before the altar, and sent for those in the citadel.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-32]
2 Maccabees 15:32
He displayed the defiled Nicanor’s head and the blasphemer’s hand, which he had stretched out against the holy house of the Almighty while boasting.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-33]
2 Maccabees 15:33
He cut out the impious Nicanor’s tongue and said that it should be given piece by piece to the birds, and that the rewards of his folly should be hung opposite the temple.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-34]
2 Maccabees 15:34
They all blessed the manifested Lord toward heaven, saying, “Blessed is He who has preserved His own place undefiled.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-35]
2 Maccabees 15:35
He hung Nicanor’s head from the citadel as an evident and visible sign to everyone of the Lord’s help.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-36]
2 Maccabees 15:36
By a common vote they all decreed that this day must never be left unmarked, but that they should specially observe the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, called Adar in the Syrian language, one day before Mordecai’s day.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-37]
2 Maccabees 15:37
Since the matters concerning Nicanor unfolded in this way, and from that time the city was held by the Hebrews, I too will end my account here.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-38]
2 Maccabees 15:38
If it is well composed and to the point, that is what I myself desired; if it is slight and mediocre, that is what I could achieve.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT 2-maccabees-section-15-v15-39]
2 Maccabees 15:39
For drinking wine by itself, and likewise water by itself, is harmful; but just as wine mixed with water is sweet and produces a delightful pleasure, so the arrangement of the account delights the ears of those who encounter the composition. Here shall be the end.
[/UNIT]

=== Ezra ===

--- Ezra 1 ---

[UNIT ezra-section-1-v1-1]
Ezra 1:1

[/UNIT]

[UNIT ezra-section-1-v1-2]

“Thus says Cyrus king of the Persians: The Lord, God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and He has charged me to build Him a house in Jerusalem in Judea.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ezra-section-1-v1-3]
Ezra 1:3
Who among you belongs to any of His people? His God will be with him, and he will go up to Jerusalem in Judea. Let him build the house of the God of Israel—He is the God in Jerusalem.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ezra-section-1-v1-4]
Ezra 1:4
As for everyone left behind, from whatever place he resides in, the men of his place will take him up with silver, gold, belongings and livestock, together with the freewill offering for the house of God in Jerusalem.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ezra-section-1-v1-5]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT ezra-section-1-v1-7]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT ezra-section-1-v1-11]

[UNIT ezra-section-4-v4-12]

[UNIT ezra-section-4-v4-13]

[UNIT ezra-section-4-v4-14]

[/UNIT]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT ezra-section-4-v4-16]
Ezra 4:16

[UNIT ezra-section-4-v4-20]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT ezra-section-4-v4-22]

--- Ezra 9 ---

[UNIT ezra-section-9-v9-1]
Ezra 9:1
When these things were completed, the leaders approached me and said, “The people of Israel, the priests and the Levites have not separated themselves from the peoples of the lands in their repulsive practices: the Chanani, Ethi, Pherezi, Iebousi, Ammoni, Moabi, Moseri and Amori,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ezra-section-9-v9-2]
Ezra 9:2
because they have taken some of their daughters for themselves and their sons, and the holy seed has been led astray among the peoples of the lands. The leaders’ hand has been foremost in this covenant-breaking.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ezra-section-9-v9-3]
Ezra 9:3
When I heard this word, I tore my garments, shook with agitation, plucked hair from my head and beard, and sat quietly.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ezra-section-9-v9-4]
Ezra 9:4
Everyone who pursued the word of the God of Israel gathered to me because of the deported community’s covenant-breaking, while I sat quietly until the evening sacrifice.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ezra-section-9-v9-5]
Ezra 9:5
At the evening sacrifice I rose from my humiliation. As I tore my garments, I shook with agitation; I bend upon my knees and stretch out my hands toward the Lord God,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ezra-section-9-v9-6]
Ezra 9:6
and said, “Lord, I am ashamed and abashed to lift my face toward Thee, for our lawless deeds have multiplied above our heads and our offenses have grown to heaven.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ezra-section-9-v9-7]
Ezra 9:7
From the days of our fathers until this day we have been in great offense. In our lawless deeds, we, our kings and our sons have been handed over into the hand of the kings of the nations—to the sword, captivity, plunder and shame of our face—as on this day.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ezra-section-9-v9-8]
Ezra 9:8
Now the Lord our God has shown us leniency, leaving some of us for deliverance and giving us a support in the place of His sanctuary, to enlighten our eyes and give us a little revival in our slavery.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ezra-section-9-v9-9]
Ezra 9:9
For we are slaves, and in our slavery the Lord our God has not abandoned us. He has inclined mercy toward us before the kings of the Persians, to give us revival, for them to raise up the house of our God and restore its desolate places, and to give us a fence in Judah and Jerusalem.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ezra-section-9-v9-10]
Ezra 9:10
What can we say, our God, after this? For we have abandoned Thy commandments,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ezra-section-9-v9-11]
Ezra 9:11
which Thou gavest us through Thy servants the prophets, saying, ‘The land you are entering to inherit is a land being moved amid the movement of the peoples of the nations, in their repulsive practices, with which they have filled it from mouth to mouth in their uncleanness.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ezra-section-9-v9-12]
Ezra 9:12
Now do not give your daughters to their sons, and do not take some of their daughters for your sons. You shall never seek their peace or good, so that you may become strong, eat the good things of the land and bequeath it to your sons for ever.’
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ezra-section-9-v9-13]
Ezra 9:13
After everything that has come upon us through our evil deeds and our great offense—for there is none like our God, because Thou hast lightened our lawless deeds and given us deliverance—
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ezra-section-9-v9-14]
Ezra 9:14
for we have returned to scattering Thy commandments and intermarrying with the peoples of the lands. Do not be provoked against us to the point of destruction, so that no remnant or survivor remains.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT ezra-section-9-v9-15]
Ezra 9:15
Lord, God of Israel, Thou art righteous, for we have been left as survivors, as on this day. Here we are before Thee in our offenses, for because of this there is no standing before Thee.”
[/UNIT]

=== Nehemiah ===

--- Nehemiah 1 ---

[UNIT nehemiah-section-1-v1-1]
Nehemiah 1:1
The words of Neemias son of Achalia. In the month of Chaseelou, in the twentieth year, I was in Sousan abira,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-1-v1-2]
Nehemiah 1:2
and Anani, one of my brothers, came, he and men of Judah. I asked them about those who had been saved, who remained from the captivity, and about Jerusalem.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-1-v1-3]
Nehemiah 1:3
They said to me, “The remaining people who were left from the captivity there in the country are in great distress and disgrace. Jerusalem’s walls have been pulled down, and its gates have been set ablaze with fire.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-1-v1-4]
Nehemiah 1:4
When I heard these words, I sat down and wept, and mourned for days. I was fasting and praying before the God of heaven,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-1-v1-5]
Nehemiah 1:5
and said, “No, I pray, Lord, God of heaven, the Mighty One, the Great and Fearsome, who dost keep the covenant and mercy for those who love Him and keep His commandments:
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-1-v1-6]
Nehemiah 1:6
let Thine ear be attentive and Thine eyes opened to hear Thy servant’s prayer, which I pray before Thee today, day and night, for the sons of Israel, Thy servants. I confess concerning the sins of the sons of Israel that we have sinned against Thee. I and my father’s house have sinned.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-1-v1-7]
Nehemiah 1:7
We have utterly broken faith with Thee, and have not kept the commandments, ordinances and judgments that Thou didst command Moses Thy servant.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-1-v1-8]
Nehemiah 1:8
Remember, I pray, the word that Thou didst command Moses Thy servant, saying, ‘If you break covenant, I will scatter you among the peoples;
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-1-v1-9]
Nehemiah 1:9
and if you turn back to Me, keep My commandments and do them, even if your dispersed people are at the farthest edge of heaven, I will gather them from there and bring them into the place I chose for My name to dwell there.’
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-1-v1-10]
Nehemiah 1:10
They are Thy servants and Thy people, whom Thou didst redeem by Thy great power and Thy mighty hand.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-1-v1-11]
Nehemiah 1:11
No, I pray, Lord! But let Thine ear be attentive to Thy servant’s prayer and to the prayer of Thy servants who wish to fear Thy name. Grant, I pray, Thy servant success today, and give him compassion before this man.” Now I was the king’s cupbearer.
[/UNIT]

--- Nehemiah 2 ---

[UNIT nehemiah-section-2-v2-1]
Nehemiah 2:1
In the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of King Arthasastha, the wine was before me. I took the wine and gave it to the king, and there was no other person before him.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-2-v2-2]
Nehemiah 2:2
The king said to me, “Why is your face distressed when you are not unwell? This is nothing but distress of heart.” I became very greatly afraid.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-2-v2-3]
Nehemiah 2:3
I said to the king, “May the king live for ever! Why should my face not be distressed, since the city, the home of my fathers’ tombs, has been laid waste and its gates have been consumed by fire?”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-2-v2-4]
Nehemiah 2:4
The king said to me, “What are you asking for?” I prayed to the God of heaven,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-2-v2-5]
Nehemiah 2:5
and said to the king, “If it pleases the king, and if your servant finds favor before you, send him to Judah, to the city of my fathers’ tombs, and I will rebuild it.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-2-v2-6]
Nehemiah 2:6
The king and the concubine sitting beside him said to me, “How long will your journey last, and when will you return?” It pleased the king, and he sent me, and I gave him a time limit.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-2-v2-7]
Nehemiah 2:7
I said to the king, “If it pleases the king, let him give me letters to the governors beyond the river, so that they may conduct me through until I reach Judah,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-2-v2-8]
Nehemiah 2:8
and a letter to Asaph, keeper of the king’s park, so that he may give me timber to roof the gates, for the city wall, and for the house I will enter.” The king granted it to me, according to the good hand of God.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-2-v2-9]
Nehemiah 2:9
I came to the governors beyond the river and gave them the king’s letters. The king had sent army commanders and horsemen with me.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-2-v2-10]
Nehemiah 2:10
Sanaballat the Aroni and Tobia the Ammoni servant heard, and it displeased them that a man had arrived to seek good for the sons of Israel.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-2-v2-11]
Nehemiah 2:11
I came to Jerusalem and was there for three days.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-2-v2-12]
Nehemiah 2:12
I arose at night, with a few men accompanying me. I told no one what God was putting into my heart to do with Israel. No animal was with me except the animal on which I was riding.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-2-v2-13]
Nehemiah 2:13
I went out through the gate of Golela, toward the mouth of the Spring of Figs and to the Dung Gate. I was breaking at Jerusalem’s wall, which they were pulling down, and its gates had been consumed by fire.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-2-v2-14]
Nehemiah 2:14
I passed on to the gate of Ain and the King’s Pool, but there was no room for the animal beneath me to pass.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-2-v2-15]
Nehemiah 2:15
I went up along the wall of the torrent at night, breaking at the wall. I was at the Valley Gate, and returned.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-2-v2-16]
Nehemiah 2:16
The guards did not know why I had gone or what I was doing. Until then I had told nothing to the Jews, the priests, the honored men, the commanders, or the remaining people who were doing the works.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-2-v2-17]
Nehemiah 2:17
I said to them, “You see the distress we are in, how Jerusalem is desolate and its gates have been given to fire. Come, let us rebuild Jerusalem’s wall, and we will no longer be a disgrace.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-2-v2-18]
Nehemiah 2:18
I told them about the hand of God, which was good upon me, and the king’s words that he had spoken to me. I said, “Let us arise and build,” and their hands were strengthened for good.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-2-v2-19]
Nehemiah 2:19
Sanaballat the Aroni, Tobia the Ammoni servant, and Gesam the Arabi heard. They laughed at us and came against us, and said, “What is this thing you are doing? Are you revolting against the king?”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-2-v2-20]
Nehemiah 2:20
I answered them and said, “The God of heaven, He will grant us success. We are His pure servants, and we will build. But you have no share, right, or memorial in Jerusalem.”
[/UNIT]

[/UNIT]

Nehemiah 3:2

[UNIT nehemiah-section-3-v3-4]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-3-v3-5]
Nehemiah 3:5
Next to them the Thekoin took charge, but the adoreem did not bring their necks into their service.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-3-v3-6]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-3-v3-8]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-3-v3-9]
Nehemiah 3:9

[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-3-v3-10]
Nehemiah 3:10

[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-3-v3-11]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-3-v3-12]
Nehemiah 3:12

[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-3-v3-13]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-3-v3-14]
Nehemiah 3:14
Melchia son of Rechab, ruler of the district of Bethacharm, repaired the Dung Gate, he and his sons. They covered it and set up its doors, locks and bars,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-3-v3-15]
Nehemiah 3:15

[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-3-v3-16]
Nehemiah 3:16
After him Neemias son of Azabouch, ruler of half the district of Bethsour, repaired as far as the garden of David’s tomb, as far as the pool that had been made, and as far as Bethaggabarim.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-3-v3-17]
Nehemiah 3:17
After him the Levites—Raoum son of Bani—repaired. Next to him Asabia, ruler of half the district of Keila, repaired for his district.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-3-v3-18]
Nehemiah 3:18
After him their brothers—Beni son of Enadad, ruler of half the district of Keila—repaired.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-3-v3-19]
Nehemiah 3:19
Next to him Azour son of Iesous, ruler of Masphe, repaired a second section of the tower of the ascent adjoining the corner.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-3-v3-20]
Nehemiah 3:20
After him Barouch son of Zabou repaired a second section, from the corner to the entrance of Bethelisoub of the high priest.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-3-v3-21]
Nehemiah 3:21
After him Meramoth son of Ouria son of Akos repaired a second section, from the entrance of Bethelisoub to the end of Bethelisoub.

[UNIT nehemiah-section-3-v3-22]
Nehemiah 3:22
After him the priests, men of Achechar, repaired.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-3-v3-23]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-3-v3-24]
Nehemiah 3:24

[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-3-v3-25]
Nehemiah 3:25
of Phalal son of Euzai, opposite the corner, and the upper tower projecting from the king’s house, belonging to the court of the guard. After him was Phadaia son of Phoros.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-3-v3-26]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-3-v3-27]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-3-v3-30]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-3-v3-31]

After him Melchia son of Saraphi repaired as far as Bethanathinim; and the dealers in small wares, opposite the gate of Maphekad and as far as the ascent of the bend.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-3-v3-32]
Nehemiah 3:32
In the intervening space at the ascent of the Sheep Gate, the metalworkers and dealers in small wares repaired.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-3-v3-33]
Nehemiah 3:33
When Sanaballat heard that we were building the wall, it displeased him. He became very angry and laughed at the Jews.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-3-v3-34]
Nehemiah 3:34
He said before his brothers, “Is this the strength of Somoron, that these Jews are building their own city?”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-3-v3-35]
Nehemiah 3:35
Tobias the Ammanite came beside him, and they said to one another, “Surely they will not sacrifice or eat in their place? Will not a fox climb up and pull down their stone wall?”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-3-v3-36]
Nehemiah 3:36
Hear, our God, for we have become an object of mockery. Turn their reproach back upon their own heads, and give them over to mockery in a land of captivity,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-3-v3-37]
Nehemiah 3:37
and do not cover over lawlessness.
[/UNIT]

--- Nehemiah 4 ---

[UNIT nehemiah-section-4-v4-1]
Nehemiah 4:1
When Sanaballat, Tobia, the Arabs and the Ammanites heard that growth had risen on Jerusalem’s walls, that the breaches were beginning to be blocked, it seemed very bad to them.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-4-v4-2]
Nehemiah 4:2
They all gathered together to come and draw up for battle in Jerusalem.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-4-v4-3]
Nehemiah 4:3
We prayed to our God and stationed outposts against them day and night because of them.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-4-v4-4]
Nehemiah 4:4
Judah said, “The strength of the enemies has been crushed. There is much rubble, and we will not be able to build the wall.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-4-v4-5]
Nehemiah 4:5
Those who were afflicting us said, “They will neither know nor see until we come among them, murder them, and bring the work to a stop.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-4-v4-6]
Nehemiah 4:6
When the Jews who lived beside them came, they told us, “They are coming up against us from every place.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-4-v4-7]
Nehemiah 4:7
I stationed people in the lowest parts of the place behind the wall, in the sheltered areas. I stationed the people by local groups, with their swords, their spears and their bows.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-4-v4-8]
Nehemiah 4:8
I looked, arose, and said to the honored men, the commanders and the rest of the people, “Do not be afraid of them. Remember our God, great and fearsome, and draw up for battle for your brothers, your sons and daughters, your wives and your houses.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-4-v4-9]
Nehemiah 4:9
When our enemies heard that it had become known to us, and God had scattered their counsel, we all returned to the wall, each to his work.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-4-v4-10]
Nehemiah 4:10
From that day on, half of those who had been shaken out did the work, and half of them held firm. Spears, shields, bows and breastplates were there, and the leaders were behind all the house of Judah,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-4-v4-11]
Nehemiah 4:11
those building on the wall. Those carrying with lifting gear were armed; with one hand each did the work itself, and the other held a dart.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-4-v4-12]
Nehemiah 4:12
The builders worked with each man’s sword girded at his waist, and the one sounding the horn was beside him.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-4-v4-13]
Nehemiah 4:13
I said to the honored men, the leaders and the rest of the people, “The work is widespread and great, and we are scattered along the wall, each far from his brother.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-4-v4-14]
Nehemiah 4:14
At whatever place you hear the sound of the horn, gather to us there, and our God will wage war for us.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-4-v4-15]
Nehemiah 4:15
We continued doing the work, while half of them held spears from the rising of dawn until the stars came out.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-4-v4-16]
Nehemiah 4:16
At that time I told the people, “Lodge within Jerusalem, and let the night be a watch for you, and the day, work.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-4-v4-17]
Nehemiah 4:17
I was there, with the men of the guard behind me, and not one of us took off his clothes.
[/UNIT]

--- Nehemiah 5 ---

[UNIT nehemiah-section-5-v5-1]
Nehemiah 5:1
A great outcry arose from the people and their wives against their Jewish brothers.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-5-v5-2]
Nehemiah 5:2
Some said, “With our sons and daughters we are many. We must obtain grain, eat, and live.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-5-v5-3]
Nehemiah 5:3
Others said, “Our fields, our vineyards and our houses—we are pledging them. We must obtain grain and eat.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-5-v5-4]
Nehemiah 5:4
Others said, “We borrowed silver for the king’s taxes—our fields, vineyards and houses are at stake.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-5-v5-5]
Nehemiah 5:5
Now our flesh is like our brothers’ flesh, and our sons like their sons. Yet we are forcing our sons and daughters into slavery, and some of our daughters are being subjected. There is no power in our hands, and our fields and vineyards belong to the honored men.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-5-v5-6]
Nehemiah 5:6
I was deeply grieved when I heard their outcry and these words.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-5-v5-7]
Nehemiah 5:7
My heart took counsel within me. I contended with the honored men and leaders and said to them, “You are making demands, each against his brother!” I brought a great assembly against them,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-5-v5-8]
Nehemiah 5:8
and said to them, “We have bought our Jewish brothers who were being sold to the nations, of our own free will. And are you selling your brothers?” They fell quiet and found no answer.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-5-v5-9]
Nehemiah 5:9
I said, “What you are doing is not good. Not so! In the fear of our God you shall depart from the reproach of the nations, our enemies.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-5-v5-10]
Nehemiah 5:10
My brothers, my acquaintances and I have also put silver and grain at their disposal. Let us, I pray, relinquish this exaction.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-5-v5-11]
Nehemiah 5:11
Please restore to them this very day their fields, vineyards, olive trees and houses; and from the silver, bring out for them the grain, wine and oil.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-5-v5-12]
Nehemiah 5:12
They said, “We will return it and ask nothing from them. We will do as you say.” I called the priests and made them swear to act according to this word.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-5-v5-13]
Nehemiah 5:13
I shook out my wrap and said, “So may God shake out from his house and his labor every man who does not uphold this word. So shall he be shaken out and empty.” All the assembly said, “Amen,” and praised the Lord. The people carried out this word.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-5-v5-14]
Nehemiah 5:14
From the day he appointed me to be their ruler in the land of Judah—from the twentieth year to the thirty-second year of Arthasastha, twelve years—I and my brothers did not eat their coerced provision,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-5-v5-15]
Nehemiah 5:15
and as for the former exactions, which before me they laid heavily upon them: they took from them bread and wine, and, at the last, silver—forty didrachms. Their shaken-out men exercise authority over the people, but I did not act that way, because of the fear of God.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-5-v5-16]
Nehemiah 5:16
I did not take charge of the work on their wall; I acquired no field, and all those gathered there were for the work.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-5-v5-17]
Nehemiah 5:17
At my table were the Jews, one hundred and fifty men, and those who came to us from the nations around us.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-5-v5-18]
Nehemiah 5:18
Each day one young bull, six choice sheep and a he-goat were prepared for me. Every ten days there was wine in abundance for everyone. Along with these things, I did not demand bread from coercion, because the service weighed heavily on this people.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-5-v5-19]
Nehemiah 5:19
Remember me for good, God, for everything I have done for this people.
[/UNIT]

--- Nehemiah 6 ---

[UNIT nehemiah-section-6-v6-1]
Nehemiah 6:1
When Sanaballat, Tobia, Gesam the Arabi and the rest of our enemies heard that I had built the wall, no breath was left in them. Up to that time I had not set doors in the gates.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-6-v6-2]
Nehemiah 6:2
Sanaballat and Gesam sent to me, saying, “Come, let us gather together in the villages in the plain of Ono.” They were planning to do me harm.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-6-v6-3]
Nehemiah 6:3
I sent messengers to them, saying, “I am doing a great work and will not be able to come down, lest the work stop. When I finish it, I will come down to you.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-6-v6-4]
Nehemiah 6:4
They sent me this same message, and I sent them an answer accordingly.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-6-v6-5]
Nehemiah 6:5
Sanaballat sent his servant to me with an open letter in his hand.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-6-v6-6]
Nehemiah 6:6
In it was written: “It has been reported among the nations that you and the Jews are planning to revolt. That is why you are building the wall, and you are becoming their king.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-6-v6-7]
Nehemiah 6:7
Besides this, you have appointed prophets for yourself so that you may sit in Jerusalem as king in Judah. Now these words will be reported to the king. Come now, let us take counsel together.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-6-v6-8]
Nehemiah 6:8
I sent to him, saying, “Nothing like these words you say has happened. You are falsely devising them from your own heart.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-6-v6-9]
Nehemiah 6:9
For they are all frightening us, saying, “Their hands will grow slack from this work, and it will not be done.” Now I strengthened my hands.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-6-v6-10]
Nehemiah 6:10
I entered the house of Semei son of Dalaia son of Meetabel, who was confined. He said, “Let us gather in the house of God, inside it, and shut its doors, for they are coming at night to murder you.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-6-v6-11]
Nehemiah 6:11
I said, “Who is the man who could enter the house and live?”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-6-v6-12]
Nehemiah 6:12
I recognized that God had not sent him, because the prophecy was a word against me, and Tobias and Sanaballat had hired
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-6-v6-13]
Nehemiah 6:13
a crowd against me, so that I might be afraid, act in that way and sin, and become a bad name for them to reproach me.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-6-v6-14]
Nehemiah 6:14
Remember, God, Tobia and Sanaballat according to these deeds of his, and Noadia the prophet and the rest of the prophets who were frightening me.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-6-v6-15]
Nehemiah 6:15
The wall was completed on the twenty-fifth of Eloul, in fifty-two days.

[/UNIT]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-9-v9-30]

[UNIT nehemiah-section-9-v9-33]

=== Esther ===

--- Esther 1 ---

[UNIT esther-section-1-v1-1]

[UNIT esther-section-1-v1-1b]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-1-v1-3]

There were gold and silver couches on a pavement of emerald stone, pearly stone, and Parian stone, and transparent coverings adorned with varied flowers, with roses scattered all around.

[UNIT esther-section-1-v1-10]

[UNIT esther-section-1-v1-12]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-1-v1-13]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-1-v1-14]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-1-v1-15]
Esther 1:15
and reported to him, according to the laws, how Queen Astin must be dealt with, because she had not done what the king commanded through the eunuchs.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-1-v1-16]
Esther 1:16

[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-1-v1-17]
Esther 1:17
(for he had recounted to them the queen’s words and how she had contradicted the king). Just as she contradicted King Artaxerxes,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-1-v1-18]
Esther 1:18
so today the other noblewomen, wives of the rulers of Persia and Media, on hearing what she said to the king, will likewise dare to dishonor their husbands.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-1-v1-19]
Esther 1:19
If, therefore, it pleases the king, let him issue a royal command, and let it be written according to the laws of Media and Persia. Let him not act otherwise, and let the queen no longer enter his presence; let the king give her royal position to a woman better than she.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-1-v1-20]
Esther 1:20
Let the law that the king makes be heard in his kingdom, and thus all the women will bestow honor on their own husbands, from poor to rich.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-1-v1-21]
Esther 1:21
The proposal pleased the king and the rulers, and the king did as Muchaeus said.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-1-v1-22]
Esther 1:22
He sent throughout his kingdom, territory by territory, according to their own language, so that they would have fear in their own households.

[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-2-v2-8]

[UNIT esther-section-2-v2-9]

[UNIT esther-section-2-v2-10]

[UNIT esther-section-2-v2-11]

[UNIT esther-section-2-v2-12]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-2-v2-13]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-2-v2-14]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-2-v2-15]
Esther 2:15
When the time was completed for Esther daughter of Aminadab, the brother of Mordecai’s father, to enter the king’s presence, she disregarded none of the instructions the eunuch, the guardian of the women, gave her. For Esther was finding favor with everyone who saw her.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-2-v2-16]
Esther 2:16
Esther entered the presence of King Artaxerxes in the twelfth month, which is Adar, in the seventh year of his reign.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-2-v2-17]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-2-v2-18]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-2-v2-19]
Esther 2:19
Mordecai was serving in the court.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-2-v2-20]

Esther did not disclose her homeland. For Mordecai had instructed her in this way: to fear God and carry out His commands, as when she was with him. Esther did not change her way of life.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-2-v2-21]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-2-v2-22]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-2-v2-23]

--- Esther 3 ---

[UNIT esther-section-3-v3-1]
Esther 3:1

[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-3-v3-2]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-3-v3-3]
Esther 3:3

[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-3-v3-4]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-3-v3-5]
Esther 3:5
When Haman learned that Mordecai did not bow before him, he became exceedingly angry
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-3-v3-6]
Esther 3:6

[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-3-v3-7]
Esther 3:7
He made a decree in the twelfth year of Artaxerxes’s reign and cast lots, day by day and month by month, to destroy Mordecai’s race in a single day. The lot fell on the fourteenth of the month, which is Adar.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-3-v3-8]
Esther 3:8
He spoke to King Artaxerxes, saying, “There is a nation scattered among the nations throughout your kingdom. Their laws are unlike those of all the nations; they disobey the king’s laws, and it is not advantageous for the king to let them be.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-3-v3-9]
Esther 3:9
If it pleases the king, let him decree their destruction, and I will pay ten thousand talents of silver into the king’s treasury.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-3-v3-10]
Esther 3:10
The king removed his ring and put it into Haman’s hand to seal the written measures against the Jews.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-3-v3-11]
Esther 3:11
The king said to Haman, “Keep the silver; deal with the nation as you wish.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-3-v3-12]
Esther 3:12
The king’s scribes were summoned on the thirteenth of the first month. As Haman commanded, they wrote to the generals and rulers in every territory from India to Ethiopia, the hundred and twenty-seven territories, and to the rulers of the nations in their own language, by authority of King Artaxerxes.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-3-v3-13]
Esther 3:13
Letters were sent by couriers into Artaxerxes’s kingdom to wipe out the race of the Jews in a single day of the twelfth month, which is Adar, and to plunder their possessions.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-3-v3-13a]
Esther 3:13a
This is the copy of the letter: “The great King Artaxerxes writes the following to the rulers of the hundred and twenty-seven territories from India to Ethiopia and to the district governors subject to them:
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-3-v3-13b]
Esther 3:13b
Having ruled many nations and gained control of the whole inhabited world, I have wished—not exalting myself through the boldness of authority, but always conducting myself with greater fairness and gentleness—to establish the lives of my subjects in perpetual calm, to provide a civilized kingdom open to travel to its furthest limits, and to renew the peace desired by all people.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-3-v3-13c]
Esther 3:13c
When I asked my counselors how this might be brought to completion, Haman, who excels among us in sound judgment, has demonstrated unchanging goodwill and firm loyalty, and has received the second honor in the kingdom,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-3-v3-13d]
Esther 3:13d
pointed out to us that among all the tribes throughout the inhabited world a certain hostile people is intermingled, opposed in its laws to every nation, continually disregarding the kings’ decrees so as not to accept the shared administration that we direct blamelessly.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-3-v3-13e]
Esther 3:13e
We have therefore understood that this nation alone stands in continual opposition to every person, differing through its strange observance of laws, showing ill will toward our affairs, and accomplishing the worst evils so that the kingdom may not enjoy stability.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-3-v3-13f]
Esther 3:13f
We have therefore commanded that all those indicated to you in the writings of Haman, who is appointed over our affairs and is our second father, be destroyed root and branch, with wives and children, by the swords of their enemies, without any pity or sparing, on the fourteenth of the twelfth month, Adar, of the present year,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-3-v3-13g]
Esther 3:13g
so that those hostile both formerly and now may go down violently to Hades in a single day and thereafter leave our affairs stable and undisturbed for all time.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-3-v3-14]
Esther 3:14
The copies of the letters were posted in every territory, and all the nations were ordered to be ready for that day.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-3-v3-15]
Esther 3:15
The matter was also hurried forward in Susa. The king and Haman were drinking heavily, while the city was troubled.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-4-v4-9]

[UNIT esther-section-4-v4-10]

[/UNIT]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-4-v4-12]
Esther 4:12
Achrathaeus reported all Esther’s words to Mordecai.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-4-v4-13]

[UNIT esther-section-4-v4-14]
Esther 4:14
For if you refuse to listen at this time, help and shelter will come to the Jews from elsewhere, but you and your father’s house will perish. Who knows whether you became queen for this time?’”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-4-v4-15]
Esther 4:15
Esther sent the man who had come to her back to Mordecai, saying:
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-4-v4-16]
Esther 4:16
“Go, assemble the Jews in Susa, and all of you fast for me. Neither eat nor drink for three days, night and day; I and my maids will also go without food. Then I will enter the king’s presence contrary to the law, even if I must perish.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-4-v4-17]
Esther 4:17
Mordecai went and did everything Esther commanded him,
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-4-v4-17a]
Esther 4:17a
and he implored the Lord, remembering all the Lord’s works, and said:
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-4-v4-17b]
Esther 4:17b
“Lord, Lord, King who dost rule over all, everything is under Thine authority, and no one can oppose Thee when Thou wishest to save Israel.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-4-v4-17c]
Esther 4:17c
For Thou madest heaven and earth and every wonderful thing beneath heaven. Thou art Lord of all, and no one can stand against Thee, the Lord.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-4-v4-17d]
Esther 4:17d
Thou knowest all things. Thou knowest, Lord, that it was not in insolence, arrogance, or love of glory that I did this, refusing to bow before arrogant Haman. For I would gladly have kissed the soles of his feet for Israel’s salvation.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-4-v4-17e]
Esther 4:17e
But I did this so that I would not set a human being’s glory above God’s glory. I will bow to no one except Thee, my Lord, and I will not do these things in arrogance.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-4-v4-17f]
Esther 4:17f
Now, Lord God, King, God of Abraham, spare Thy people, for they look upon us to destroy us and have desired to destroy Thine inheritance from the beginning.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-4-v4-17g]
Esther 4:17g
Do not overlook Thy portion, which Thou didst redeem for Thyself from the land of Egypt.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-4-v4-17h]
Esther 4:17h
Hear my supplication, be gracious to Thine allotted people, and turn our mourning into feasting, so that while living we may sing hymns to Thy name, Lord. Do not wipe out the mouth of those who praise Thee.”
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-4-v4-17i]
Esther 4:17i
All Israel cried out with all their strength, because their death was before their eyes.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-4-v4-17k]
Esther 4:17k
Queen Esther took refuge in the Lord, gripped by mortal anguish. She took off her glorious garments and put on garments of distress and mourning. Instead of splendid perfumes she filled her head with ashes and dung, greatly humbled her body, and filled every place of her joyful adornment with her tangled hair. She implored the Lord God of Israel and said:
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-4-v4-17l]
Esther 4:17l
“My Lord, our King, Thou art the only one. Help me, who am alone and have no helper except Thee, for my danger is at hand.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-4-v4-17m]
Esther 4:17m
From my birth I have heard within my ancestral tribe that Thou, Lord, didst take Israel from all the nations and our fathers from all their ancestors as an everlasting inheritance, and do for them everything Thou saidst.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-4-v4-17n]
Esther 4:17n
Now we have sinned before Thee, and Thou hast handed us over to our enemies because we glorified their gods. Thou art righteous, Lord.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT esther-section-4-v4-17o]

=== Job ===

--- Job 1 ---

[UNIT job-section-1-v1-4]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT job-section-1-v1-5]

For Job said, “Perhaps my sons have conceived evil thoughts toward God in their minds.” So Job did this continually.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT job-section-1-v1-13]

[/UNIT]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT job-section-1-v1-16]

[/UNIT]

[UNIT job-section-1-v1-17]
Job 1:17

[/UNIT]

[UNIT job-section-1-v1-18]

[/UNIT]

--- Psalms 1 ---

[UNIT psalms-section-1-v1-1]

and did not sit in the seat of pestilent men;
[/UNIT]

[UNIT psalms-section-1-v1-2]

but his will is in the Lord’s law,
and on His law he will meditate day and night.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT psalms-section-1-v1-3]

He will be like the tree planted beside the outlets of waters,
which will give its fruit in its season,
and whose leaf will not fall off;
and everything he does will be prospered.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT psalms-section-1-v1-4]
Psalms 1:4
Not so the ungodly, not so,
but like chaff which the wind flings away from the face of the earth.
[/UNIT]

[UNIT psalms-section-1-v1-5]
Psalms 1:5
Therefore the ungodly will not rise in judgment,
nor sinners in the council of the righteous;
[/UNIT]

[UNIT psalms-section-1-v1-6]
Psalms 1:6
for the Lord knows the way of the righteous,
and the way of the ungodly will perish.
[/UNIT]
